knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normality inside the group generated by the affine semigroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An affine semigroup \(S\) is normal if it is integrally closed in its generated group: for every \(x\in\operatorname{gp}(S)\) and every integer \(k\ge1\), the implication
\[kx\in S\quad\Longrightarrow\quad x\in S\]
holds. The ambient group is essential. Normality does not require inclusion of lattice points lying outside \(\operatorname{gp}(S)\), even when those points belong to the real cone generated by \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine semigroup is normal when any group element whose positive multiple lies in the semigroup already belongs to the semigroup.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Semigroup Normality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly states normality relative to the generated group and fits the terminal container, but no supporting citation is supplied.

children.title: Semigroup Saturation
children.top_down_role: Completeness of a semigroup within its ambient lattice cone.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The saturation of \(S\) is \(\overline S=\{x\in\operatorname{gp}(S):kx\in S\text{ for some }k\ge1\}=\operatorname{cone}(S)\cap\operatorname{gp}(S)\).

notation.meaning: The saturation of the affine semigroup.

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Saturation relative to the semigroup's generated group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The saturation of \(S\) is
\[\overline S:=\{x\in\operatorname{gp}(S):kx\in S\text{ for some }k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\}.\]
For a finitely generated affine semigroup this set also has the geometric representation
\[\overline S=\operatorname{cone}(S)\cap\operatorname{gp}(S).\]
Thus saturation adjoins precisely the group-lattice points in the rational cone of \(S\) whose positive multiples already occur in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The saturation consists of generated-group elements having a positive multiple in the semigroup; equivalently, it is the generated group intersected with the real cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Semigroup Saturation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The saturation definition and cone-intersection representation are consistent, but the geometric equality requires an inspectable affine-semigroup reference.

children.title: Normality-Saturation Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between normal generation and lattice saturation.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finitely generated affine semigroup.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\text{ is normal}\Longleftrightarrow S=\overline S\Longleftrightarrow S=\operatorname{cone}(S)\cap\operatorname{gp}(S)\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence of algebraic normality and geometric lattice saturation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finitely generated affine semigroup \(S\), the following conditions are equivalent: \(S\) is normal in \(\operatorname{gp}(S)\); \(S\) equals its saturation \(\overline S\); and
\[S=\operatorname{cone}(S)\cap\operatorname{gp}(S).\]
Consequently, if \(S=\mathbb{N}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\), normality is equivalent to the generators \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\) forming a Hilbert basis of their cone relative to the lattice \(\operatorname{gp}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely generated affine semigroup is normal exactly when it equals both its saturation and the generated-group lattice points in its cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Normality-Saturation Correspondence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind and equivalences fit the correspondence leaf, but neither the normality-saturation equivalence nor its Hilbert-basis consequence has a cited locator.

children.title: Semigroup Holes
children.top_down_role: Missing lattice points in cone-semigroup generation.

assumptions_latex: \(S\) is an affine semigroup with saturation \(\overline S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hole set is \(H(S)=\overline S\setminus S\), and \(S\) is normal exactly when \(H(S)=\varnothing\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Holes measured relative to the generated group, not an arbitrary ambient lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A hole of \(S\) is an element of its saturation that is absent from the semigroup. The hole set is therefore
\[H(S):=\overline S\setminus S=\bigl(\operatorname{cone}(S)\cap\operatorname{gp}(S)\bigr)\setminus S.\]
Every \(h\in H(S)\) has some positive integral multiple in \(S\), but \(h\notin S\). The equality \(H(S)=\varnothing\) holds exactly when \(S\) is normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A semigroup hole is a generated-group lattice point in the semigroup's cone that does not belong to the semigroup itself.
knowledge_statements.title: Semigroup Holes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generated-group-relative definition of holes is precise and appropriate, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Nonnormal Affine Semigroups
children.top_down_role: Affine semigroups failing normal generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnormal Affine Semigroups
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete hole-based predicate for failure of affine-semigroup normality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The affine semigroup \(S\) is nonnormal if and only if there exist \(x\in\operatorname{gp}(S)\) and \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge2}\) such that \(kx\in S\) but \(x\notin S\). Equivalently,
\[H(S)=\overline S\setminus S\ne\varnothing.\]
Thus a single hole certifies nonnormality. Conversely, every failure of the defining normality implication produces an element of \(H(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finitely generated affine semigroup is nonnormal exactly when it has a hole, equivalently when some absent group element has a positive multiple in the semigroup.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finitely generated affine semigroup.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\) is nonnormal exactly when \(\overline S\setminus S\ne\varnothing\).

children.title: Hole-Structure Regimes

assumptions_latex: Affine semigroups are considered inside their generated groups.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Semigroup hole sets may be empty, finite nonempty, or infinite; nonnormality alone does not determine their size.

notation.meaning: The numerical semigroup generated by \(2\) and \(3\).
A two-dimensional affine semigroup with infinitely many holes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete boundary between finite-hole and infinite-hole nonnormal semigroups.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Hole sets exhibit distinct regimes. The normal case has no holes. For \(S_1=\mathbb{N}\{2,3\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}\), one has \(\overline S_1=\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) and \(H(S_1)=\{1\}\), so the hole set is finite and nonempty. For \(S_2=\mathbb{N}\{(2,0),(0,1),(1,1)\}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^2\), one has \(\overline S_2=\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}^2\), while every \((2r+1,0)\) with \(r\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\) is a hole. Hence nonnormal affine semigroups can have either finitely or infinitely many holes.

children.title: Integer Decomposition Property
children.top_down_role: Discrete decomposition structure of dilated integral polyhedra.

assumptions_latex: \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a lattice polytope with respect to a lattice \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) has IDP exactly when \(kP\cap L=(P\cap L)+\cdots+(P\cap L)\) for every integer \(k\ge1\).

notation.meaning: The set of lattice points of \(P\).

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer decomposition for lattice polytopes and all positive integral dilations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The lattice polytope \(P\) has the integer decomposition property if, for every integer \(k\ge1\) and every lattice point \(z\in kP\cap L\), there exist \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\in P\cap L\) such that
\[z=z_1+\cdots+z_k.\]
Equivalently, for every \(k\ge1\),
\[kP\cap L=\underbrace{(P\cap L)+\cdots+(P\cap L)}_{k\text{ summands}}.\]
The dilation is scalar dilation about the origin; the definition is invariant under lattice translation of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lattice polytope has IDP when every lattice point in every positive integer dilation decomposes into that many lattice points of the original polytope.
knowledge_statements.title: Integer Decomposition Property

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise, quantifies every positive dilation, and matches the IDP leaf, but no authoritative section, definition, theorem, or page locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Middle integer decomposition property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the middle integer decomposition property and records that it implies ordinary integer decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) has the middle integer decomposition property if, for every \(k\in\mathbb N\) and every \(c\in\mathbb Z^n\), the polyhedron
\[
P\cap(c-kP)
\]
is integral. Every polyhedron with the middle integer decomposition property has the integer decomposition property; thus, for each \(k\in\mathbb N\) and \(c\in kP\cap\mathbb Z^n\), there exist \(c_1,\ldots,c_k\in P\cap\mathbb Z^n\) with \(c=c_1+\cdots+c_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedron has the middle integer decomposition property when every intersection with an integral translate of a negative integer dilation is integral. This stronger property implies the ordinary integer decomposition property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall k\in\mathbb N\ \forall c\in\mathbb Z^n,\ P\cap(c-kP)\text{ is integral}\bigr]\Rightarrow\operatorname{IDP}(P).

children.title: Integer Rounding Property
children.top_down_role: Rounding compatibility in integral covering and packing systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Rounding Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covering-form integer rounding property with a unit-cost multiplier formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{Z}^{m\times n}\). The system associated with \(A\) has the integer rounding property if, for every \(c\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) for which the displayed minima are finite, \[\min\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}y:y\in\mathbb{Z}_+^m,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\}=\left\lceil\min\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}y:y\in\mathbb{R}_+^m,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\ge c\}\right\rceil.\] Thus restricting the covering multipliers to integers changes the continuous optimum only by upward rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer covering multipliers attain exactly the ceiling of the continuous unit-cost covering optimum for every integral demand vector having a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{IP}}(c)=\lceil z_{\mathrm{LP}}(c)\rceil\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covering-form definition is plausible, but no inspectable source establishes this exact sign, feasibility, and unit-cost convention for the integer rounding property.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Blocking and anti-blocking characterizations of integer rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes integer rounding for nonnegative integral covering and packing systems using decomposition properties and extremal integral rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be a nonnegative integral matrix. For \(P_{\ge}:=\{x\ge0\mid Ax\ge\mathbf1\}\), the system \(x\ge0,\ Ax\ge\mathbf1\) has the integer rounding property if and only if its blocking polyhedron \(B(P_{\ge})\) has the integer decomposition property and every componentwise-minimal integral vector of \(B(P_{\ge})\) is a row of \(A\). For \(P_{\le}:=\{x\ge0\mid Ax\le\mathbf1\}\), the system \(x\ge0,\ Ax\le\mathbf1\) has the integer rounding property if and only if its anti-blocking polyhedron \(A(P_{\le})\) has the integer decomposition property and every componentwise-maximal integral vector of \(A(P_{\le})\) is a row of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative integral matrix, the covering system has integer rounding exactly when its blocking polyhedron has integer decomposition and all its minimal integral vectors occur as rows of the matrix. Dually, the packing system has integer rounding exactly when its anti-blocking polyhedron has integer decomposition and all its maximal integral vectors occur as rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{IRP}(x\ge0,Ax\ge\mathbf1)\iff\bigl(\operatorname{IDP}(B(P_{\ge}))\land\operatorname{Min}(B(P_{\ge})\cap\mathbb Z^n)\subseteq\operatorname{rows}(A)\bigr),\quad \operatorname{IRP}(x\ge0,Ax\le\mathbf1)\iff\bigl(\operatorname{IDP}(A(P_{\le}))\land\operatorname{Max}(A(P_{\le})\cap\mathbb Z^n)\subseteq\operatorname{rows}(A)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer round-down and round-up properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the covering and packing specializations of the integer rounding property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(A\) has the integer round-down property if the system \(x\ge0,\ Ax\ge\mathbf1\) has the integer rounding property. It has the integer round-up property if the system \(x\ge0,\ Ax\le\mathbf1\) has the integer rounding property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The integer round-down property means that the associated nonnegative covering system has integer rounding. The integer round-up property means that the associated nonnegative packing system has integer rounding.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: TDI and Hilbert-basis characterization of integer rounding
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes integer rounding through a homogenized TDI system and an equivalent Hilbert-basis condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Ax\le b\) be a feasible rational system with \(b\in\mathbb Z^m\). Then \(Ax\le b\) has the integer rounding property if and only if
\[
Ax-b\eta\le0,\qquad \eta\ge0
\]
is TDI, where \(\eta\) is a new variable. Equivalently, the rows of
\[
\begin{bmatrix}A&b\\0&1\end{bmatrix}
\]
form a Hilbert basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a feasible rational system with integral right-hand side, integer rounding is equivalent to total dual integrality of its homogenized system and to the augmented matrix rows forming a Hilbert basis.
assumptions_latex: Ax\le b\text{ is a feasible rational system}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{IRP}(Ax\le b)\iff\bigl(Ax-b\eta\le0,\ \eta\ge0\text{ is TDI}\bigr)\iff\operatorname{rows}\!\begin{bmatrix}A&b\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\text{ form a Hilbert basis}.

knowledge_statements.title: Normal Lattice Polytopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normality expressed as decomposition of lattice points in every positive integral dilation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A lattice polytope \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is normal if, for every integer \(k\ge1\) and every \(z\in kP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\), there exist \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\in P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\) such that \[z=z_1+\cdots+z_k.\] Equivalently, the affine semigroup generated by \(\{(x,1):x\in P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\}\) contains every lattice point in the cone over \(P\) at positive integral height.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every lattice point in every integral dilation of a normal lattice polytope decomposes into that many lattice points of the original polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(kP\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d)+\cdots+(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^d)\) with \(k\) summands

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposition Failure Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reeve tetrahedra exhibit failure of degree-two lattice-point decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(m\ge2\), let \(R_m=\operatorname{conv}\{(0,0,0),(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(1,1,m)\}\). Its only lattice points are its four vertices, while \((1,1,1)\in2R_m\cap\mathbb{Z}^3\). No two lattice points \(u,v\in R_m\cap\mathbb{Z}^3\) satisfy \(u+v=(1,1,1)\). Hence \(R_m\) lacks the integer decomposition property and is not normal.

children.title: Closure Invariance
children.top_down_role: Closure behavior under transformations expected to preserve the represented set.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Invariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order invariance for a closure defined by simultaneous intersection of generated cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), and let \(\mathcal H(P)\) be a set of closed halfspaces generated from \(P\). Define \(C(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal H(P)}H\). For every enumeration \((H_i)_{i\in I}\) of \(\mathcal H(P)\) and every bijection \(\pi:I\to I\), \[P\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}H_i=P\cap\bigcap_{i\in I}H_{\pi(i)}=C(P).\] Therefore a simultaneous one-round closure is invariant under reordering or duplicating its defining cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closure formed by intersecting all generated halfspaces is unchanged when those halfspaces are reordered or repeated.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H(P)\) is fixed as a set of halfspaces
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(P)\) is invariant under permutations and repetitions of \(\mathcal H(P)\)

notation.meaning: Halfspaces generated for P in one closure round

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order and repetition invariance is correct for a fixed simultaneous intersection and the property kind fits, but no source with a specific locator is provided.

children.title: Closure Monotonicity
children.top_down_role: Closure behavior under containment relations among input sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Monotonicity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order preservation of a set-based closure operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A closure map \(C\) on a family \(\mathcal P\) of subsets of \(\mathbb{R}^d\) is monotone if, for all \(P,Q\in\mathcal P\), \[P\subseteq Q\quad\Longrightarrow\quad C(P)\subseteq C(Q).\] For a cutting-plane closure, this implication requires the cut-generation rule to be inclusion-compatible; validity of each generated inequality alone does not ensure monotonicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monotone closure preserves set inclusion; establishing this for a cutting closure requires an inclusion-compatible cut-generation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(P)\subseteq C(Q)\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity formula is precise, but the additional assertion about inclusion-compatible cut generation is nontrivial and unsupported by an inspectable citation.

children.title: Representation-Sensitive Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of invariance when equivalent sets receive different descriptions.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation-Sensitive Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between set-defined and formulation-defined cutting closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_1\) and \(R_2\) be two finite inequality systems with the same feasible relaxation \(P\), and let \(C_{\mathrm{rep}}(R)\) intersect cuts generated from the displayed rows of \(R\). Representation invariance fails precisely when equivalent descriptions can generate unequal intersections: \[\{x\in P:x\text{ satisfies every cut generated from }R_1\}\ne\{x\in P:x\text{ satisfies every cut generated from }R_2\}.\] A closure is set-invariant only when its generated intersection depends on \(P\), not on the chosen rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A formulation-based closure is representation-sensitive when two equivalent inequality descriptions generate different one-round intersections.
assumptions_latex: Cuts may depend on displayed rows
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_{\mathrm{rep}}(R_1)\ne C_{\mathrm{rep}}(R_2)\) is the representation-sensitivity witness

notation.meaning: Closure generated from the particular representation R

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The witness condition fits a representation-sensitivity failure boundary, but no concrete closure family or source verifies the claimed boundary in the intended cutting-plane setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Polyhedrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-generation criterion for a one-round halfspace closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a polyhedron and \(C(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal H(P)}H\). If there is a finite subfamily \(H_1,\ldots,H_t\in\mathcal H(P)\) such that \[P\cap\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal H(P)}H=P\cap H_1\cap\cdots\cap H_t,\] then \(C(P)\) is a polyhedron. Conversely, when \(C(P)\) is polyhedral, finite describability does not by itself ensure that its facets belong to the original generated family without an additional finite-basis property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite subset of generated cuts defining the entire closure guarantees polyhedrality; the converse needs an additional finite-basis condition.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H(P)\) is a family of closed halfspaces
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C(P)=P\cap H_1\cap\cdots\cap H_t\Longrightarrow C(P)\text{ is polyhedral}\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-subfamily implication is correct, and the converse caveat is appropriately restrained, but the finite-basis boundary lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Closure Strength Order
children.top_down_role: Relative strength among closure families.

children.title: Closure Dominance
children.top_down_role: Relative strength ordering among closure operators.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Dominance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise strength order between two closure operators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) be closure maps defined on the same family \(\mathcal P\) of relaxations. The closure \(C_1\) dominates \(C_2\) on \(\mathcal P\) if \[C_1(P)\subseteq C_2(P)\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal P.\] Dominance is strict if this inclusion is strict for at least one \(P\in\mathcal P\). Under the minimization-relaxation convention, the smaller closed set is the stronger closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One closure dominates another when it produces a subset for every relaxation, with strict dominance if some inclusion is proper.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\succeq C_2\iff(\forall P\in\mathcal P)\ C_1(P)\subseteq C_2(P)\)

notation.meaning: C1 dominates C2 in closure strength

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly expresses pointwise closure dominance and fits the terminal container, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Closure Inclusions
children.top_down_role: Set-containment relations among closure outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Inclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut implication as a sufficient condition for closure inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i\in\{1,2\}\), let \(C_i(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal H_i(P)}H\). If every point of \(C_1(P)\) satisfies every halfspace in \(\mathcal H_2(P)\), then \[C_1(P)\subseteq C_2(P).\] In particular, the inclusion holds whenever \(\mathcal H_2(P)\subseteq\mathcal H_1(P)\). Thus containment of cut families reverses to containment of their closed feasible regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If all cuts defining the second closure are implied by the first closure, then the first closed region is contained in the second.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1(P)\subseteq C_2(P)\)

notation.meaning: Cut halfspaces defining closure i at P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cut-implication argument and reversal of cut-family containment are correct, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Closure Incomparability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where closure families admit no uniform strength ordering.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Incomparability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Witness criterion for failure of a uniform closure-strength order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a family of subsets of \(\mathbb R^d\), and let \(C_1,C_2:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P\) be closure maps. They are incomparable on \(\mathcal P\) if there exist \(P,Q\in\mathcal P\) and \(x,y\in\mathbb R^d\) such that \[x\in C_1(P)\setminus C_2(P),\qquad y\in C_2(Q)\setminus C_1(Q).\] The first witness rules out \(C_1(R)\subseteq C_2(R)\) for every \(R\in\mathcal P\), and the second rules out \(C_2(R)\subseteq C_1(R)\) for every \(R\in\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two closures are incomparable when separate instances witness failure of each possible universal inclusion direction.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is a family of subsets of \(\mathbb R^d\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\not\succeq C_2\) and \(C_2\not\succeq C_1\)

notation.meaning: C1 dominates C2 when its value is contained in C2's value on every relaxation

children.title: Closure Access Problem Pair
children.top_down_role: Computational access to implicitly represented closures.

children.title: Closure Membership
children.top_down_role: Decision access for points relative to implicitly represented closures.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Membership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision formulation of access to a specified one-round closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational description of a relaxation \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), a rational point \(x\in\mathbb{Q}^d\), and a specified cut family \(\mathcal H(P)\). Define \(C(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{H\in\mathcal H(P)}H\). The closure-membership problem outputs YES exactly when \[x\in P\quad\text{and}\quad x\in H\text{ for every }H\in\mathcal H(P),\] and outputs NO otherwise. A NO answer may be certified by a violated defining inequality or generated cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a relaxation, point, and cut family, decide whether the point satisfies the relaxation and every cut defining its closure.
assumptions_latex: The closure family \(\mathcal H(P)\) is specified
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{MEM}_C(P,x)=\mathrm{YES}\iff x\in C(P)\)

notation.meaning: Closure of P under the specified cuts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decision formulation fits closure membership, but an arbitrary specified cut family need not have a finite encoding or checkable violated-cut certificate. A family-specific computational model and source are required.

children.title: Closure Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation access for points lying outside a closure.

knowledge_statements.title: Closure Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Search formulation of access to a specified one-round closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational description of \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), a rational point \(x\in\mathbb Q^d\), and a specified closure \(C(P)\). A separation algorithm either certifies \(x\in C(P)\), or returns \(a\in\mathbb Q^d\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb Q\) satisfying \[a^{\mathsf T}z\le\beta\quad\text{for every }z\in C(P),\qquad a^{\mathsf T}x>\beta.\] When separation is restricted to the generating cut family, the returned halfspace must additionally belong to that family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either certify that a point belongs to the closure or return a rational inequality valid for the closure and violated by the point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in C(P)\), or \(a\in\mathbb Q^d\) and \(\beta\in\mathbb Q\) are returned with \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le\beta<a^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(z\in C(P)\)

notation.meaning: Coefficients of the returned separating inequality

children.title: Oracle-Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Computational relationships or gaps between membership and separation access.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between weak, well-bounded oracle equivalence and unrestricted exact closure access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nonempty convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) supplied with rational inner- and outer-radius bounds and a requested rational tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), weak membership and weak separation are polynomial-time Turing reducible to one another, with complexity polynomial in the encoding length and \(\log(1/\varepsilon)\). This equivalence does not extend automatically to exact closure access: absent quantitative well-boundedness and an approximation convention, an exact membership oracle alone need not provide a polynomial-time exact separation procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak membership and separation are polynomially equivalent for well-bounded convex sets with tolerances; exact membership alone does not generally yield efficient exact separation.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty, convex, and quantitatively well bounded.
\(\varepsilon>0\) is rational and encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathrm{WMEM}_{\varepsilon}(C)\equiv_T^{\mathrm{poly}}\mathrm{WSEP}_{\varepsilon}(C)\), whereas unrestricted exact membership does not imply polynomial-time exact separation.

notation.meaning: weak membership oracle at tolerance epsilon
weak separation oracle at tolerance epsilon

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weak-oracle equivalence requires an authoritative theorem specifying the well-boundedness parameters and tolerance transformations; equivalence at the identical epsilon is not established. The asserted failure of exact membership-to-separation reduction also needs a precise model and source.

children.title: Representation Dependence
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity to aggregation, extension, and formulation choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intrinsic closure invariance versus possible strengthening after closure in an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), the intrinsic Chvátal–Gomory closure \(P'\), obtained from every integral normal and its support value over \(P\), depends only on \(P\), not on a particular inequality description. If a rational polyhedron \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+k}\) satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=P\), then \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q')\subseteq P'\), because every intrinsic cut for \(P\) lifts with zero auxiliary-variable coefficients. The inclusion can be strict; hence closing an extended formulation and then projecting may be stronger than closing the projected formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intrinsic CG closure is description invariant, but applying closure before projecting an extended formulation can yield a strictly stronger relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P'\) is intrinsic and \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q')\subseteq P'\), with strict inclusion possible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Description invariance and the non-strict projection inclusion are plausible, but strict inclusion needs a sourced example. The closure applied to Q must also specify which auxiliary coordinates are integer-constrained.

children.title: Chvátal–Gomory Closure Polyhedrality
children.top_down_role: Polyhedrality of the elementary closure across standard regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Closure Polyhedrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-round intrinsic closure of a rational polyhedron in pure-integer space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a rational polyhedron and define its Chvátal–Gomory closure by \[P'=\bigcap_{c\in\mathbb{Z}^n:\,h_P(c)<+\infty}\left\{x\in P:c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lfloor h_P(c)\rfloor\right\},\qquad h_P(c)=\sup_{y\in P}c^{\mathsf T}y.\] Although the displayed intersection ranges over infinitely many integral vectors, \(P'\) is a rational polyhedron. Equivalently, finitely many Chvátal–Gomory inequalities suffice to describe the complete one-round closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The one-round Chvátal–Gomory closure of every rational polyhedron is itself a rational polyhedron and has a finite inequality description.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P'\) is a rational polyhedron describable by finitely many Chvátal–Gomory inequalities.

notation.meaning: support value of P in direction c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is an appropriately placed polyhedrality theorem and is mathematically standard, but no inspectable theorem or section locator supports it.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Rational polyhedrality of the Chvátal closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedrality under the section's standing rational-polyhedron setup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a rational polyhedron, then its Chvátal closure \(P^{Ch}\) is a rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Chvátal closure of a rational polyhedron is itself a rational polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a rational polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P^{Ch}\text{ is a rational polyhedron}.

children.title: Chvátal–Gomory Rank
children.top_down_role: Iteration depth for inequalities, relaxations, and integer-hull recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranks of valid inequalities and of pure-integer rational relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(P^{(0)}=P\) and recursively let \(P^{(t+1)}=(P^{(t)})'\). For an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) valid for \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n)\), its Chvátal–Gomory rank relative to \(P\) is the least \(t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}\) for which it is valid for \(P^{(t)}\), or \(+\infty\) if none exists. The rank of \(P\) is the least \(t\) satisfying \(P^{(t)}=P_I\), with the same infinity convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: CG rank is the minimum number of closure rounds needed to validate an integer-hull inequality or recover the entire integer hull.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{CG}(a,\beta;P)=\min\{t:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for }P^{(t)}\}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}_{CG}(P)=\min\{t:P^{(t)}=P_I\}\).

notation.meaning: convex hull of the integer points of P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and definitions fit the rank container, but the record supplies no source locator for the conventions governing inequality rank, relaxation rank, and infinite rank.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Chvátal rank and strong Chvátal rank of a rational matrix
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines matrix-level ranks uniformly over all integral right-hand sides.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}$ and, for each $b\in\mathbb{Z}^m$, let $P_b=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\le b\}$. The Chvátal rank of $A$ is the least $t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ such that $P_b^{(t)}=(P_b)_I$ for every $b\in\mathbb{Z}^m$, where $P_b^{(t)}$ is the $t$-fold Chvátal closure and $(P_b)_I=\operatorname{conv}(P_b\cap\mathbb{Z}^n)$. The strong Chvátal rank of $A$ is the Chvátal rank of $\begin{bmatrix}I\\-I\\A\\-A\end{bmatrix}$. For rational $A$, both ranks are well-defined finite integers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a rational matrix A, its Chvátal rank is the smallest nonnegative number of Chvátal-closure rounds that recovers the integer hull for every integral right-hand side. Its strong Chvátal rank is the Chvátal rank of the matrix obtained by stacking I, −I, A, and −A. Both ranks are finite integers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{Ch}}(A)=\min\{t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}:P_b^{(t)}=(P_b)_I\ \forall b\in\mathbb{Z}^m\},\qquad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{sCh}}(A)=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{Ch}}\!\left(\begin{bmatrix}I\\-I\\A\\-A\end{bmatrix}\right)<\infty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empty integer hull forces a recession-dimension drop
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession geometry of a nonempty rational polyhedron whose affine hull contains an integer point but whose integer hull is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty rational polyhedron such that \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n\ne\varnothing\), and let \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb Z^n)\). If \(P_I=\varnothing\), then \(\dim(\operatorname{rec}(P))<\dim(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a nonempty rational polyhedron has an integer point in its affine hull but no integer point in the polyhedron itself, its recession cone has strictly smaller dimension than the polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a nonempty rational polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \dim(\operatorname{rec}(P))<\dim(P).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integral inequality representation of the integer hull
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An integral description within the affine hull using nonorthogonal normals that also support valid inequalities for the original polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty rational polyhedron with \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n\ne\varnothing\), and let \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb Z^n)\). There exist an integral matrix \(A\) and an integral vector \(b\) such that \[P_I=\{x:Ax\le b\}\cap\operatorname{aff}(P).\] For every row \(a^i\) of \(A\), the vector \(a^i\) is not orthogonal to \(\operatorname{aff}(P)\), and there is \(d_i\in\mathbb R\) such that \(a^ix\le d_i\) is valid for \(P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within its affine hull, the integer hull has a description by integral inequalities. Each selected normal is nonorthogonal to the affine hull and is also the normal of some inequality valid for the original polyhedron.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a nonempty rational polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n},\ b\in\mathbb Z^m:\ P_I=\{x:Ax\le b\}\cap\operatorname{aff}(P),\quad \forall i,\ a^i\not\perp\operatorname{aff}(P),\quad \exists d_i\in\mathbb R\text{ such that }a^ix\le d_i\text{ is valid for }P.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterated Chvátal closures and Chvátal rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions of inequality and polyhedron rank, finite convergence for rational pure-integer polyhedra, and the mixed-integer failure boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polyhedron, \(S=P\cap\mathbb Z^n\), and \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Define \(P^{(1)}=P^{Ch}\) and \(P^{(t)}=(P^{(t-1)})^{Ch}\) for integers \(t\ge2\). An inequality valid for \(P^{(t)}\) but not for \(P^{(t-1)}\) has Chvátal rank \(t\). There exists a finite \(T\) such that \(P^{(T)}=P_I\), and the least such \(T\) is the Chvátal rank of \(P\). Thus every inequality valid for \(P_I\) becomes valid after finitely many iterations. This finite-convergence assertion is for the pure-integer case and can fail in the mixed-integer setting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly applying the Chvátal closure yields a nested sequence. An inequality's rank is the iteration at which it first becomes valid, and the polyhedron's rank is the first iteration equal to its pure-integer hull. This rank is finite for rational pure-integer polyhedra, whereas analogous mixed-integer convergence can fail.
assumptions_latex: P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is a rational polyhedron}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists T<\infty\text{ such that }P^{(T)}=P_I;\quad \operatorname{rank}_{Ch}(P)=\min\{T:P^{(T)}=P_I\}.

children.title: Chvatal-Function Integer-Duality Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Functional representations connecting rounding closure and integer duality.

children.title: Chvátal-Function Representations
children.top_down_role: Functional descriptions associated with iterated rounding structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal-Function Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive finite expressions encoding repeated nonnegative aggregation and integer rounding.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An affine Chvátal function on \(\mathbb{R}^n\) is represented by a finite rooted expression tree whose leaves are rational affine functions and whose internal nodes apply addition, multiplication by a nonnegative rational scalar, or the ceiling operator. Thus every such function has a finite expression formed recursively from \(x\mapsto a^{\mathsf T}x+b\), with \(a\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb{Q}\). The ceiling depth is the largest number of ceiling nodes on a root-to-leaf path and records the nested rounding depth of the representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Affine Chvátal functions are finite rational-affine expression trees using nonnegative aggregation and ceilings; tree depth records nested rounding.
assumptions_latex: \(a\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}\), and scalar multipliers are nonnegative rationals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) admits a finite representation generated from rational affine leaves by \((f,g)\mapsto f+g\), \(f\mapsto\lambda f\), and \(f\mapsto\lceil f\rceil\), where \(\lambda\in\mathbb{Q}_{+}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the container, but the allowed scalar signs and the stated ceiling-depth convention vary across definitions of affine Chvátal functions and require a specific source.

children.title: Integer-Duality Interpretations
children.top_down_role: Dual viewpoints for integer optimization systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Duality Interpretations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite CG derivations interpreted as dual certificates for bounded pure-integer linear optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z_I=\max\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\leq b,\ x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\}\), where the data are rational, the feasible set is nonempty, and \(z_I\) is finite. A finite sequence of nonnegative aggregations and valid integer roundings deriving \(c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is an integer-dual certificate with value \(\beta\). Weak duality gives \(z_I\leq\beta\). Finite Chvátal–Gomory convergence for rational polyhedra yields a certificate with \(\beta=z_I\); consequently, minimizing the certified bound over all finite derivations gives the integer optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite aggregation-and-rounding derivations act as integer-dual certificates, and the best certified bound equals the bounded pure-integer optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b,c\) are rational and all variables are integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_I=\min\{\beta:c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\text{ has a finite Chvátal–Gomory derivation from }Ax\leq b\}\).

notation.meaning: upper bound certified by a finite derivation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact equality between the optimum and the best finite derivation depends on the formal derivation system and scaling conventions. With rational c, the treatment of a nonintegral objective row must be stated and supported; finite closure convergence alone does not fix these conventions.

children.title: Rounding-Duality Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural correspondence between Chvátal-function rounding and integer duality.

knowledge_statements.title: Rounding-Duality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-round CG cuts as rounded dual aggregations of a linear inequality system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b\}\). For every multiplier \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}A\in\mathbb{Z}^{1\times n}\), linear-programming weak duality gives \((\lambda^{\mathsf T}A)x\leq\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\) for all \(x\in P\). On integer points the left side is integral, so the strengthened inequality \[(\lambda^{\mathsf T}A)x\leq\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\] is valid. Conversely, every system-form one-round Chvátal–Gomory cut is obtained from such a nonnegative dual aggregation followed by rounding of its right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-round CG cut is exactly a nonnegative dual aggregation with integral coefficients followed by rounding down the aggregated right side.
assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) is a rational linear system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda^{\mathsf T}A)x\leq\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\) is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\) and represents a system-form CG cut.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rounded nonnegative-aggregation rule is standard and fits the duality interface, but the claimed converse characterization of every system-form one-round CG cut has no source locator.

children.title: System-Form Variants
children.top_down_role: Chvátal–Gomory closure behavior across alternative linear-system forms.

knowledge_statements.title: System-Form Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unified CG aggregation rule for inequality and equality rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax\leq b,\ Ex=f\}\), choose \(\lambda\geq0\) and a free multiplier \(\mu\) such that \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}A+\mu^{\mathsf T}E\in\mathbb{Z}^{1\times n}\). Then \[(\lambda^{\mathsf T}A+\mu^{\mathsf T}E)x\leq\left\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\mu^{\mathsf T}f\right\rfloor\] is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\). Reversing a greater-than row changes its sign, and replacing an equality by its two opposite inequalities yields the same family because every free multiplier is a difference of two nonnegative multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inequalities use nonnegative multipliers, equalities use free multipliers, and standard sign or equality conversions preserve the resulting CG-cut family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed rounded aggregation is valid, and equivalent sign/equality system forms generate the same system-form CG cuts.

children.title: Convex-Set Extensions
children.top_down_role: Extensions of the closure beyond rational polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Set Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function definition of CG closure for arbitrary convex sets in pure-integer space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a convex set \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), define \(h_K(c)=\sup\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in K\}\). Its Chvátal–Gomory closure is \[\operatorname{CG}(K)=K\cap\bigcap_{c\in\mathbb{Z}^n:\,h_K(c)<+\infty}\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:c^{\mathsf T}x\leq\lfloor h_K(c)\rfloor\right\}.\] Every inequality in the intersection is valid for \(K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\), since its left-hand side is integral there. Directions having infinite support impose no cut. This definition remains meaningful without assuming that \(K\) is polyhedral or rational.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The CG closure of any convex set intersects all integral-normal support inequalities after rounding finite support values downward.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\subseteq\operatorname{CG}(K)\subseteq K\).

notation.meaning: support value of K in integral direction c

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The extension is plausible, but conventions differ on whether the closure explicitly intersects K and on assumptions such as closedness. A source is needed to validate the stated arbitrary-convex-set version.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cut closures and the split closure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines elementary and iterated cut closures, specializes them to split cuts, and records rational polyhedrality of the one-round split closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a polyhedron \(P\) and a class \(\mathcal C\) of cutting planes, the \(\mathcal C\)-closure of \(P\) is obtained by applying every cut in \(\mathcal C\) to \(P\). The elementary closure applies the cuts directly to \(P\) without reoptimization after cuts are added, whereas the rank-\(k\) closure recursively adds cuts and reoptimizes for \(k\) rounds. If \(\mathcal C\) is the class of cuts obtained from integral split disjunctions \(\pi x\leq\pi_0\ \vee\ \pi x\geq\pi_0+1\), then the resulting closure is the split closure. If \(P\) is a rational polyhedron, its split closure is a rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut-class closure imposes all cuts from that class. The elementary closure applies them without intermediate reoptimization, while a rank-k closure repeats cut addition and reoptimization for k rounds. For integral split disjunctions this is the split closure, which is a rational polyhedron whenever the original polyhedron is rational.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal C\text{ is a class of cutting planes applicable to }P
P\text{ is rational for the polyhedrality conclusion}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\text{ rational}\implies \operatorname{SC}(P)\text{ is a rational polyhedron}.

children.title: Split-Disjunction Geometry
children.top_down_role: Slab geometry and integer-coordinate structure underlying split closures.

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Disjunction Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive integer slabs for a designated set of integer coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) index the integer-constrained coordinates. A split disjunction is \[\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\leq\pi_0\quad\vee\quad\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\geq\pi_0+1,\] where \(\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^{I}\) is primitive and nonzero and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb{Z}\). Its excluded open slab \(\{x:\pi_0<\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I<\pi_0+1\}\) contains no point whose coordinates indexed by \(I\) are integral. For a convex relaxation \(P\), the associated split relaxation is the convex hull of the portions of \(P\) lying in the two closed halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split removes the open unit-width slab between two consecutive integer hyperplanes and convexifies the two surviving portions of the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\leq\pi_0\})\cup(P\cap\{\pi^{\mathsf T}x_I\geq\pi_0+1\})\bigr)\) preserves every mixed-integer point of \(P\).

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. The Convex Hull of a Disjunctive Set p. 17

children.title: Split-Closure Polyhedrality

knowledge_statements.title: Split-Closure Polyhedrality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite describability of the one-round split closure of a rational mixed-integer polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a rational polyhedron and let \(I\) index its integer-constrained variables. For every split \((\pi,\pi_0)\), let \(P^{\pi,\pi_0}\) be the convex hull of the two portions of \(P\) satisfying the corresponding disjunction. The split closure \[\operatorname{SC}(P)=\bigcap_{\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^{I}\setminus\{0\},\,\pi_0\in\mathbb{Z}}P^{\pi,\pi_0}\] is a rational polyhedron. Hence the intersection over the infinite family of split disjunctions admits a finite rational inequality description.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The one-round split closure of a rational mixed-integer polyhedron is a rational polyhedron despite being defined by infinitely many splits.
assumptions_latex: \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) is the fixed integer-variable index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{SC}(P)\) is a rational polyhedron.

notation.meaning: disjunctive relaxation associated with one split

children.title: Split Rank
children.top_down_role: Iteration depth associated with split-derived strengthening.

knowledge_statements.title: Split Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranks of valid inequalities and relaxations under iterated split closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(P^{[0]}=P\) and recursively define \(P^{[t+1]}=\operatorname{SC}(P^{[t]})\). For an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) valid for the mixed-integer hull \(P_I\), its split rank relative to \(P\) is the least \(t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}\) for which it is valid for \(P^{[t]}\), or \(+\infty\) if no finite round suffices. The split rank of \(P\) is the least \(t\) such that \(P^{[t]}=P_I\), again with value \(+\infty\) when equality never occurs finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split rank counts closure rounds needed to establish an inequality or recover the mixed-integer hull, and it may be infinite.
assumptions_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for its mixed-integer hull \(P_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{rank}_{S}(a,\beta;P)=\min\{t:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for }P^{[t]}\}\) and \(\operatorname{rank}_{S}(P)=\min\{t:P^{[t]}=P_I\}\), using \(+\infty\) when necessary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the rank container, but the fixed integer-variable set underlying SC and the mixed-integer hull should be explicit. No source locator establishes the stated rank conventions, including infinite relaxation rank.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Split rank of a relaxation and a valid inequality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines split rank, including nonfinite rank, and records the stated finiteness regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P^k\) be the \(k\)-fold split closure of a relaxation \(P\) of \(S\). If such a nonnegative integer exists, the split rank of \(P\) is \(\min\{k:P^k=\operatorname{conv}(S)\}\). For an inequality \(\alpha x\leq\beta\) valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(S)\), its split rank is \(\min\{k:\alpha x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for }P^k\}\), when this set is nonempty; otherwise it has no finite split rank. Split rank need not be finite in general, but it is finite for pure integer programs and is at most \(|I|\) for mixed \(0,1\) linear programs with integer-variable index set \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split rank is the least number of split-closure rounds needed to reach the integer hull, or the least round at which a given valid inequality becomes valid. It can be infinite in general, is finite for pure integer programs, and is at most the number of integer variables for mixed binary linear programs.
assumptions_latex: P^k\text{ is the }k\text{-fold split closure of }P
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{split}}(P)=\min\{k:P^k=\operatorname{conv}(S)\},\qquad \operatorname{rank}_{\mathrm{split}}(\alpha x\leq\beta)=\min\{k:\alpha x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for }P^k\},\text{ when the respective minimum exists.}

children.title: Split-Closure Membership
children.top_down_role: Complexity of deciding whether a point belongs to the split closure.

assumptions_latex: The integer variables have index set \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{SC}(P)\) exactly when it belongs to every split relaxation of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact membership condition using all split disjunctions on the designated integer variables.

source_refs.locator: 10.8 The Split Closure p. 141

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^n\) with \(\pi_j=0\) for \(j\notin I\), and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb{Z}\), define \(P^{\pi,\pi_0}=\operatorname{conv}((P\cap\{x:\pi^\top x\leq\pi_0\})\cup(P\cap\{x:\pi^\top x\geq\pi_0+1\}))\). The split closure is \(\operatorname{SC}(P)=\bigcap_{\pi,\pi_0}P^{\pi,\pi_0}\). Hence the split-closure membership problem asks whether a given rational point \(\bar x\in\mathbb{Q}^n\) satisfies \(\bar x\in P^{\pi,\pi_0}\) for every admissible \((\pi,\pi_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is in the split closure precisely when it survives the convexified relaxation associated with every integer-supported split disjunction.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Closure Membership

children.title: Split-Closure Separation
children.top_down_role: Complexity of finding a violated split-closure inequality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output either certifies \(\bar x\in\operatorname{SC}(P)\) or supplies a valid inequality separating \(\bar x\) from \(\operatorname{SC}(P)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strong separation certificate for the split closure.

source_refs.locator: 10.8 The Split Closure p. 141

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The split-closure separation problem takes \(P\) and \(\bar x\) as input. It must either certify \(\bar x\in\operatorname{SC}(P)\), or return \((a,\beta)\in\mathbb{Q}^n\times\mathbb{Q}\) such that \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for every \(x\in\operatorname{SC}(P)\) while \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\). The returned inequality is a separation certificate once its validity for \(\operatorname{SC}(P)\) is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation either confirms membership or returns a rational inequality valid for the entire split closure and violated by the query point.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Closure Separation

children.title: Membership–Separation Reductions
children.top_down_role: Oracle reductions connecting the two access problems.

assumptions_latex: The split closure is a nonempty bounded rational polyhedron with known rational size bounds.
Oracle arithmetic and accuracy are measured in the standard rational bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong separation answers exact membership directly, while weak membership and weak separation are polynomial-time interreducible under the stated geometric bounds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle reductions in the bounded rational convex-body model; no unrestricted exact reverse reduction is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strong separation oracle for \(K\) decides exact membership by accepting precisely when it returns no violated valid inequality. Conversely, if rational balls \(B(c,r)\subseteq K\subseteq B(c,R)\) are known, then the standard ellipsoid reductions transform a weak membership oracle of tolerance polynomially smaller than \(\varepsilon\) into a weak separation oracle of accuracy \(\varepsilon\), and conversely, using a number of oracle calls polynomial in \(n\), the input bit length, and \(\log(R/(r\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation immediately decides membership; with bounded-body data and tolerances, weak membership and weak separation admit polynomial-time oracle reductions.
knowledge_statements.title: Membership–Separation Reductions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The strong-separation-to-membership implication is standard, but the stated bidirectional weak-oracle reduction, tolerance dependence, and bit-complexity bound require an authoritative convex-optimization source with a theorem or section locator. The complexity-bound kind fits the reduction leaf.

children.title: Infinite Split-Rank Regimes
children.top_down_role: Geometric obstructions to finite split convergence.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) has infinite split rank exactly when \(\operatorname{SC}^t(P)\neq P_I\) for every finite \(t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the infinite-rank regime; a geometric characterization requires separate authoritative evidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Set \(\operatorname{SC}^0(P)=P\) and \(\operatorname{SC}^{t+1}(P)=\operatorname{SC}(\operatorname{SC}^t(P))\) for integers \(t\geq0\). The split rank of \(P\) relative to \(P_I\) is \(\inf\{t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq0}:\operatorname{SC}^t(P)=P_I\}\), with the infimum of the empty set defined as \(+\infty\). Thus the infinite split-rank regime consists of relaxations for which every finite iterate strictly contains the mixed-integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation has infinite split rank when no finite number of split-closure rounds yields its mixed-integer hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Infinite Split-Rank Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives the formal definition of infinite split rank, but the terminal context specifically concerns geometric obstructions to finite split convergence. No source supports either the definition in this setting or the expected obstruction regime, so the appropriate mathematical scope cannot be verified.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Rounding Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure theory associated with mixed-integer rounding families.

assumptions_latex: The first \(p\) coordinates are required to be integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The MIR closure is the intersection of \(P\) with all halfspaces defined by valid MIR cuts.

notation.meaning: family of mixed-integer rounding inequalities generated from valid rows for P

knowledge_statements.scope_note: System-independent closure generated by all valid mixed-integer rounding inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{M}(P)\) contain every pair \((a,\beta)\) obtained by applying the mixed-integer rounding rule to a valid linear inequality for \(P\), respecting integrality of the first \(p\) variables. The mixed-integer rounding closure is \(\operatorname{MIR}(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in\mathcal{M}(P)}\{(x,y):a^\top(x,y)\leq\beta\}\). Every mixed-integer feasible point belongs to \(\operatorname{MIR}(P)\), and \(\operatorname{MIR}(P)\subseteq P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The MIR closure retains exactly the relaxation points satisfying every mixed-integer rounding inequality obtainable from a valid linear row.

children.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Closure
children.top_down_role: Closure structure induced by Gomory mixed-integer families.

assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a rational mixed-integer linear relaxation given by a fixed formulation with a designated integer-variable set.
GMI cuts are generated from the admissible fractional tableau rows of that fixed formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation-relative GMI closure is the intersection of \(P\) with all Gomory mixed-integer cut halfspaces generated by the specified tableau-row family.

notation.meaning: family of Gomory mixed-integer cut inequalities generated from the fixed formulation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure relative to the explicitly fixed family of admissible GMI tableau rows.

source_refs.locator: 9.4 Using Lift-and-Project to Choose the Best Mixed Integer Gomory Cut p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal{G}(P)\) be the family of inequalities \(a^\top z\leq\beta\) produced by the Gomory mixed-integer formula from the admissible fractional tableau rows of the fixed formulation of \(P\). Define \(\operatorname{GMI}(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in\mathcal{G}(P)}\{z:a^\top z\leq\beta\}\). Since every member of \(\mathcal{G}(P)\) is valid for the mixed-integer feasible set, its convex hull is contained in \(\operatorname{GMI}(P)\), and \(\operatorname{GMI}(P)\subseteq P\).

children.title: Single-Row Closures

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The single-row closure is \(C_1(P)=P\cap\bigcap_i\operatorname{conv}(P_i\cap D_I)\).

points in the common domain satisfying the integrality restrictions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Row closure relative to a fixed linear representation and common variable domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each row \(a_i^\top z\leq b_i\), retain the common domain \(D\) and impose that row alone. The single-row closure is \(C_1(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m\operatorname{conv}(P_i\cap D_I)\). Equivalently, it is the set of points of \(P\) satisfying every inequality valid for the mixed-integer set associated with one original row and the common domain. Its value may depend on the chosen representation \(Az\leq b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed formulation, the single-row closure enforces every mixed-integer consequence obtainable from each original constraint considered separately.

assumptions_latex: \(1\leq k\leq m\), and \(P_J\) retains rows indexed by \(J\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The closure \(C_k(P)\) intersects the mixed-integer hulls of all relaxations containing at most \(k\) rows.

notation.meaning: relaxation retaining rows in J and the common domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: At-most-(k\u000b)-row closure relative to a fixed formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), let \(P_J=\{z\in D:a_i^\top z\leq b_i\text{ for all }i\in J\}\). The at-most-\(k\)-row closure is \(C_k(P)=P\cap\bigcap_{J:\,1\leq|J|\leq k}\operatorname{conv}(P_J\cap D_I)\). Thus \(C_k(P)\) enforces every inequality valid for a mixed-integer relaxation formed from at most \(k\) displayed rows together with the common domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The k-row closure enforces all mixed-integer consequences obtainable from every subsystem containing at most k original constraints.

children.title: Cross-Row Strength Gaps
children.top_down_role: Structural gains available when several rows interact.

assumptions_latex: The closures \(C_k(P)) are defined from one fixed formulation with at most \(m\) rows.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_Ileq C_{k+1}(P)leq C_k(P)leq C_1(P)leq P\), and some formulations make at least one inclusion strict.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic strength hierarchy; quantitative or explicit strict-gap families remain to be sourced.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because every subsystem with at most \(k\) rows also appears among those with at most \(k+1\) rows, the associated closures satisfy \(P_I\subseteq C_{k+1}(P)leq C_k(P)leq C_1(P)leq P\). Equality is not automatic: there exist formulation families for which a point satisfies every single-row consequence but violates an inequality derivable only by jointly using multiple rows. Such a point witnesses a strict cross-row strength gap \(C_{k+1}(P)
eq C_k(P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allowing more rows cannot weaken the closure, and some formulations have points removed by multirow reasoning but retained by every single-row closure.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Row Strength Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The monotonicity direction is plausible under the preceding at-most-k-row definitions, but numerous malformed commands make the assumptions, notation, statement, and conclusion invalid. More importantly, the asserted existence of strict cross-row gaps requires an authoritative theorem or explicit sourced example. The property kind is appropriate only after that evidence is supplied.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregation closure intersects the mixed-integer hulls of all nonnegative single-row aggregations of the formulation.

notation.meaning: mixed-integer points of the common domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation closure for a fixed inequality formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(lambdainb R_+^m\), define the aggregated relaxation \(P(lambda)=xin D:lambda^top Axleqlambda^top b\}\). Its mixed-integer hull is \(H(lambda)=operatorname{conv}(P(lambda)cap D_I)bigr)\). children.title: Disjunctive Convexification Rank Pair
children.top_down_role: Rank notions induced by disjunctive convexification.

children.title: Disjunctive Rank
children.top_down_role: Depth measured through repeated disjunctive closure operations.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank of an inequality under simultaneous binary disjunctions on a zero-one relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) be a polyhedron and, for \(J\subseteq[n]\), define \(D_J(P)=\operatorname{conv}\{x\in P:x_j\in\{0,1\}\text{ for every }j\in J\}\). For an inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) valid for \(P_I=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\{0,1\}^n)\), its disjunctive rank is \[r_D(a,\beta;P)=\min\{|J|:J\subseteq[n],\ a^\top x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for }D_J(P)\}.\] The minimum of the empty set is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The disjunctive rank is the fewest binary-variable disjunctions whose simultaneous convexification makes the target inequality valid.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_D(a,\beta;P)\) is the minimum cardinality of a sufficient disjunction index set.

notation.meaning: simultaneous disjunctive convexification over indices in J

source_refs.locator: 6.1 Disjunctive Rank p. 80

children.title: Sequential-Convexification Rank
children.top_down_role: Depth measured through successive convexification stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential-Convexification Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank of an inequality under successive one-variable binary convexifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\) be a polyhedron. For every polyhedron \(Q\subseteq[0,1]^n\) and \(j\in[n]\), define \(C_j(Q)=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((Q\cap\{x:x_j=0\})\cup(Q\cap\{x:x_j=1\})\bigr)\). Given an inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\{0,1\}^n)\), define its sequential-convexification rank by \[r_S(a,\beta;P)=\min\bigl\{k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}:\exists j_1,\ldots,j_k\in[n]\text{ such that }a^\top x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for }C_{j_k}\circ\cdots\circ C_{j_1}(P)\bigr\}.\] Indices may repeat, rank zero is allowed, and the minimum of the empty set is defined as \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential-convexification rank is the minimum number of successive one-coordinate binary convexifications needed to make an inequality valid; coordinates may be selected repeatedly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_S(a,\beta;P)\) is the minimum length of a successful convexification sequence.

notation.meaning: convexification with respect to the binary disjunction on coordinate j

source_refs.locator: Chapter 3. Sequential Convexification of Disjunctive Sets p. 41

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 3. Sequential Convexification of Disjunctive Sets p. 41

children.title: Rank Correspondence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where the two depth measures coincide or diverge.

knowledge_statements.title: Rank Correspondence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality criterion for simultaneous-disjunctive and sequential-convexification ranks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\). Suppose that for every \(J=\{j_1,\ldots,j_k\}\subseteq[n]\), some ordering satisfies \(C_{j_k}\circ\cdots\circ C_{j_1}(P)=D_J(P)\). Then every inequality valid for the binary hull of \(P\) satisfies \(r_S(a,\beta;P)=r_D(a,\beta;P)\). More generally, if only \(D_J(P)\subseteq C_{j_k}\circ\cdots\circ C_{j_1}(P)\) is guaranteed, then \(r_D(a,\beta;P)\leq r_S(a,\beta;P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact equivalence of simultaneous and ordered convexifications yields equal ranks; one-sided containment yields a corresponding rank inequality.
assumptions_latex: The stated equality or containment holds for every relevant index set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under exact correspondence, \(r_S=r_D\); under the stated containment, \(r_D\leq r_S\).

children.title: Lift-Projection Rank Tradeoff

children.title: Lifted-Space Closure Depth
children.top_down_role: Rank behavior measured before eliminating auxiliary variables.

knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Space Closure Depth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closure depth measured before projecting an extended formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q^0\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\) be a lifted relaxation, let \(Q^\star\subseteq Q^0\) be its target lifted hull, and let \(\mathcal L\) be a closure operator with \(\mathcal L(Q)\subseteq Q\). Define \(Q^{t+1}=\mathcal L(Q^t)\). The lifted-space closure depth is \[d_{\mathrm{lift}}(Q^0,Q^\star;\mathcal L)=\min\{t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}:Q^t=Q^\star\},\] with value \(+\infty\) when no finite iterate equals \(Q^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lifted-space depth is the first closure round at which the extended relaxation itself equals its designated lifted hull.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal L(Q)\subseteq Q\) on the relevant lifted relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{lift}}\) is the least lifted-space iteration count attaining \(Q^\star\).

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

children.title: Projected Closure Depth
children.top_down_role: Rank behavior observed after projection to the original space.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Closure Depth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth measured by attainment of the target after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q^0\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\), let \(Q^{t+1}=\mathcal L(Q^t)\), and let \(\pi:\mathbb R^{n+m}\to\mathbb R^n\) be linear. For a target set \(P^\star\subseteq\pi(Q^0)\), the projected closure depth is \[d_{\mathrm{proj}}(Q^0,P^\star;\mathcal L,\pi)=\min\{t\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}:\pi(Q^t)=P^\star\}.\] It is \(+\infty\) if the projected iterates never equal \(P^\star\) at a finite round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected depth is the first lifted closure round whose projection equals the target set in the original variables.
assumptions_latex: \(Q^{t+1}=\mathcal L(Q^t)\) for a contracting closure operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{proj}}\) is the least iteration count attaining \(P^\star\) after projection.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 8. The Correspondence Between Lift-and-Project Cuts and Simple Disjunctive Cuts p. 97

children.title: Lift–Projection Rank Gaps
children.top_down_role: Differences caused by lifting choices, projection, or operator variants.

knowledge_statements.title: Lift–Projection Rank Gaps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison between exact attainment in a lift and after projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(Q^\star\subseteq Q^0\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+m}\), \(P^\star=\pi(Q^\star)\), and every iterate \(Q^t\) contains \(Q^\star\). Whenever \(Q^t=Q^\star\), necessarily \(\pi(Q^t)=P^\star\); hence \(d_{\mathrm{proj}}\leq d_{\mathrm{lift}}\). Define the lift–projection rank gap by \(g=d_{\mathrm{lift}}-d_{\mathrm{proj}}\) when both depths are finite. Then \(g\geq0\), and \(g>0\) precisely when projection attains the target before the lifted iterates eliminate all non-target lifted points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection can reach the original target earlier than the lift reaches its target, producing a nonnegative depth gap.
assumptions_latex: Both depths are finite when their numerical gap is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\mathrm{proj}}\leq d_{\mathrm{lift}}\) and \(g=d_{\mathrm{lift}}-d_{\mathrm{proj}}\geq0\).

children.title: Cross-Family Rank Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Relative depth and strength among closure and hierarchy families.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Family Rank Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operator-dominance principle for comparing closure ranks across families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) and \(\mathcal G\) be contracting closure operators on a common class of relaxations, and suppose \(\mathcal F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal G(Q)\) for every relaxation reachable from \(P\). Then induction gives \(\mathcal F^t(P)\subseteq\mathcal G^t(P)\) for every \(t\geq0\), provided the same containment remains applicable to the iterates. Consequently, for any target inequality valid on the common terminal hull, its validity rank satisfies \(r_{\mathcal F}\leq r_{\mathcal G}\). Equality need not follow from one-step containment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniformly stronger closure has no larger inequality rank than a weaker closure, assuming dominance persists throughout iteration.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F(Q)\subseteq\mathcal G(Q)\) on all relevant iterates.
Both rank notions use the same initial relaxation and target inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{\mathcal F}\leq r_{\mathcal G}\).

notation.meaning: t-fold iteration of closure family F
validity rank under closure family F
