children.title: Chvátal–Gomory Finite-Convergence Regime
children.top_down_role: Finite integer-hull recovery in the classical rational-polyhedral setting.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Finite-Convergence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite convergence for rational polyhedra with all variables integral.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polyhedron and define \(P^{(0)}=P\) and \(P^{(t+1)}=\operatorname{CG}(P^{(t)})\), where \(\operatorname{CG}\) denotes the Chvátal–Gomory closure. Then there exists an integer \(r\geq0\), depending on \(P\), such that \[P^{(r)}=P_I:=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb Z^n).\] Thus every rational polyhedron has finite Chvátal–Gomory rank, although the theorem does not assert a uniform dimension-independent bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated Chvátal–Gomory closure reaches the integer hull of every rational polyhedron after finitely many instance-dependent rounds.
assumptions_latex: All coordinates are subject to integrality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists r\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\) such that \(\operatorname{CG}^r(P)=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb Z^n)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-convergence theorem is standard and appropriately classified, but this nontrivial theorem has no cited source or inspectable theorem, section, or page locator.

children.title: Bounded Discrete Hierarchy Convergence
children.top_down_role: Finite-depth behavior associated with bounded binary and finite-state settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Discrete Hierarchy Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convergence of exact binary-conditioning hierarchies on bounded zero-one systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq[0,1]^n\), and let \(H^t(P)\) be a hierarchy satisfying \(H^0(P)=P\) and the following exact-conditioning property: after conditioning on any \(t\) distinct coordinates, \(H^t(P)\) contains no point outside the convex hull of the corresponding \(2^t\) binary faces of \(P\). Then \[H^n(P)=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\{0,1\}^n).\] Hence the hierarchy converges in at most \(n\) rounds. The conclusion depends on exact conditioning and does not cover arbitrary contracting closures.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A hierarchy that exactly conditions one new binary coordinate per level reaches the zero-one hull within the number of binary variables.
assumptions_latex: The hierarchy satisfies the stated exact-conditioning property for distinct coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(H^n(P)=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\{0,1\}^n)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-conditioning condition only states an upper containment and does not explicitly ensure that the hierarchy contains the zero-one hull, so equality at level n is not established. The hierarchy family and supporting source are also unspecified.

children.title: Instance-Dependent Finite Rank
children.top_down_role: Finite convergence without uniform shallow depth.

knowledge_statements.title: Instance-Dependent Finite Rank
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite rank for every instance without a uniform bound over the class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathscr P\) be a class of relaxations and let \(r_{\mathcal C}(P)\in\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\cup\{+\infty\}\) denote the rounds required by a closure family \(\mathcal C\) to reach the designated hull of \(P\). The family has instance-dependent finite rank on \(\mathscr P\) when \[r_{\mathcal C}(P)<+\infty\quad\text{for every }P\in\mathscr P,\qquad \sup_{P\in\mathscr P}r_{\mathcal C}(P)=+\infty.\] The first condition is pointwise finite convergence; the second excludes any uniform finite depth over \(\mathscr P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every individual instance converges finitely, but ranks across the instance class are unbounded.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) and the designated terminal hull are fixed on \(\mathscr P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise finiteness holds while \(\sup_{P\in\mathscr P}r_{\mathcal C}(P)=+\infty\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: quantifier-level distinction between pointwise and uniform finite convergence
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantifier-level definition is internally coherent and fits the node role, but no citation supports using this exact term for pointwise finite yet class-unbounded rank.

children.title: Rank-Growth Driver Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Rank growth associated with dimension, coefficient size, and relaxation geometry.

children.title: Dimension-Driven Rank Growth
children.top_down_role: Dependence of closure rank on ambient or formulation dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Driven Rank Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic regime where unbounded rank tracks increasing ambient or integer dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For instances \((P_k)_{k\geq1}\), let \(d_k\) be the relevant ambient or integer dimension, \(r_k\) their ranks under a fixed closure family, and \(e_k,g_k\) chosen encoding and geometric-complexity controls. Rank growth is dimension-driven relative to these controls if \[d_k\to\infty,\qquad r_k\to\infty,\qquad \sup_k e_k<\infty,\qquad \sup_k g_k<\infty.\] Any use of this classification must state the closure family and the precise definitions of \(d_k,e_k,g_k\); otherwise the attribution is not invariant under reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank growth is dimension-driven when rank and dimension diverge while stipulated encoding and geometric measures remain uniformly controlled.
assumptions_latex: A single closure family and rank convention are used for all \(P_k\).
The controls \(d_k,e_k,g_k\) are specified before classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed asymptotic predicates classify \((P_k)\) as dimension-driven relative to the chosen controls.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed condition is coherent only relative to chosen controls, but those controls lack local standardization and no source supports this diagnostic classification.

children.title: Encoding-Driven Rank Growth
children.top_down_role: Dependence of closure rank on coefficient magnitude or input length.

knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Driven Rank Growth
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic regime where rank grows with numerical encoding complexity at controlled dimension and geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For rationally encoded instances \((P_k)_{k\geq1}\), let \(L_k\) be the maximum binary encoding length of their defining rational data, \(r_k\) their ranks under a fixed closure family, and \(d_k,g_k\) selected dimension and geometric controls. Rank growth is encoding-driven relative to these controls if \[L_k\to\infty,\qquad r_k\to\infty,\qquad \sup_k d_k<\infty,\qquad \sup_k g_k<\infty.\] The encoding convention and formulation must be fixed, since rescaling or extended reformulation can change \(L_k\) without preserving this classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank growth is encoding-driven when rank and coefficient bit-length diverge while selected dimension and geometric measures stay controlled.
assumptions_latex: All instances use a fixed rational encoding convention and closure family.
The dimension and geometric controls are specified uniformly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed asymptotic predicates classify \((P_k)\) as encoding-driven relative to the chosen controls.

notation.meaning: binary encoding length of instance data

children.title: Geometry-Driven Rank Growth
children.top_down_role: Dependence of closure rank on the shape of the initial relaxation.

assumptions_latex: A closure operator \(\mathcal C\) and target hull operator \(H\) are fixed on a class of rational polyhedra.
Each family member \(P_t\) has finite rank \(r_{\mathcal C}(P_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\sup_t r_{\mathcal C}(P_t)=+\infty\quad\text{while dimension and encoding size remain uniformly bounded, with growth attributable to }g(P_t).\]

notation.meaning: Least closure round reaching the target hull
Selected geometric parameter, such as lattice width or facial configuration

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is a taxonomy condition separating geometric rank growth from dimension- and encoding-driven growth.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification predicate for parametric families, not a universal rank lower-bound theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A family \((P_t)_{t\in T}\) exhibits geometry-driven \(\mathcal C\)-rank growth when \(r_{\mathcal C}(P_t):=\min\{k\in\mathbb N_0:\mathcal C^k(P_t)=H(P_t)\}\) is unbounded, the ambient dimension and chosen rational encoding size are uniformly bounded, and a specified geometric parameter \(g(P_t)\) is unbounded or degenerates along every subsequence on which the ranks diverge. Thus the asserted driver must be stated explicitly and cannot merely restate rank, dimension, or coefficient size.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rank growth is geometry-driven when ranks become arbitrarily large despite bounded dimension and encoding size, with a separately specified geometric parameter accounting for the divergence.
knowledge_statements.title: Geometry-Driven Rank Growth

children.title: Infinite-Rank Regimes

assumptions_latex: The iterates satisfy \(P\supseteq\mathcal C(P)\supseteq\mathcal C^2(P)\supseteq\cdots\supseteq H(P)\).
The target hull \(H(P)\) is fixed by \(\mathcal C\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation \(P\), define its \(\mathcal C\)-rank relative to \(H(P)\) by \[r_{\mathcal C}(P):=\inf\{k\in\mathbb N_0:\mathcal C^k(P)=H(P)\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing:=+\infty\). The relaxation lies in an infinite-rank regime precisely when no finite closure iterate equals the target hull. This definition does not require the iterates to converge to the hull in the limit.

children.title: Finite-Stage Nonattainment

assumptions_latex: The closure iterates are nested and contain \(H(P)\).
The closure rank is measured relative to the fixed target \(H(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\forall k\in\mathbb N_0,\quad H(P)\subsetneq\mathcal C^k(P).\]

notation.meaning: The result after k closure rounds

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The condition concerns exact equality at finite rounds, independently of limiting convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite-stage nonattainment holds for \(P\) when every finite closure iterate still contains a point outside the target hull: \[\forall k\in\mathbb N_0\;\exists x_k\in\mathcal C^k(P)\setminus H(P).\] Because \(H(P)\subseteq\mathcal C^k(P)\), this is equivalent to \(H(P)\subsetneq\mathcal C^k(P)\) for every finite \(k\), and hence to \(r_{\mathcal C}(P)=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-stage nonattainment means that every finite closure iterate strictly contains the target hull, even if the excess changes from round to round.

children.title: Asymptotic Hull Approach
children.top_down_role: Limiting behavior when successive closures approach the target without finite attainment.

assumptions_latex: The sequence \((\mathcal C^k(P))_{k\ge0}\) is nested and each member is closed.
Every iterate contains the target hull \(H(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C^k(P)\ne H(P)\ \forall k<\infty,\qquad \bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}\mathcal C^k(P)=H(P).\]

notation.meaning: Limit set of the nested iterates

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Nested-set convergence is naturally represented by intersection of all finite iterates.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Setwise asymptotic attainment; it asserts neither finite convergence nor a metric convergence rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The asymptotic-hull regime for \(P\) is the conjunction of finite-stage nonattainment and exact limiting intersection: \[P_k:=\mathcal C^k(P),\qquad P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k,\qquad P_k\ne H(P)\text{ for all }k\in\mathbb N_0,\qquad \bigcap_{k=0}^{\infty}P_k=H(P).\] Thus every point outside \(H(P)\) is removed after some point-dependent finite number of rounds, although no single finite round removes all such points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The iterates never equal the hull at a finite stage, but their nested intersection is exactly the hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Hull Approach

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested-intersection representation is coherent, but whether a given closure exhibits this regime is closure-specific and no supporting source is supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Chvátal–Gomory Proof Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer rational linear systems; mixed-integer variants require a different inference rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Chvátal–Gomory derivation starts from \(Ax\le b\). If the currently available inequalities are written as \(Bx\le d\), an inference may choose \(\lambda\ge0\) such that \(c:=\lambda^{\mathsf T}B\in\mathbb Z^n\) and append \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}d\rfloor\). This inference is valid for every integral \(x\) satisfying the current premises. A validity certificate ends with the claimed inequality; an integer-infeasibility certificate ends with a contradiction such as \(0\le-1\). Each line is checkable using rational arithmetic and integrality tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Chvátal–Gomory proof repeatedly takes a nonnegative combination of the currently available inequalities whose aggregated left side is integral, rounds down the aggregated right side, and appends the result; deriving a contradiction certifies integer infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The initial system is \(Ax\le b\) with \(A,b\) rational and \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\).
Every current system \(Bx\le d\), multiplier, and derived inequality has a finite rational encoding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[0\le-1\text{ derived by the rules certifies }\{x\in\mathbb Z^n:Ax\le b\}=\varnothing.\]

notation.meaning: Nonnegative multiplier applied to the current inequalities

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The stated rounding rule is the standard Chvátal–Gomory inference for pure integer systems.

children.title: Split Proof Systems
children.top_down_role: Cutting-plane certificates derived from split disjunctions.

assumptions_latex: The variables selected by \(\pi\) are constrained to be integral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P\cap\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\in\mathbb Z\}\subseteq\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap D^-)\cup(P\cap D^+)\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Integral split vector supported on integer variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-line split inference and its use as a sequential cutting-plane certificate.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 1. Disjunctive Programming and Its Relation to Integer Programming p. 1
Chapter 2. The Convex Hull of a Disjunctive Set p. 17

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^n\) supported only on integer-constrained coordinates and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\), the split disjunction is \(D^-\cup D^+\), where \(D^-:=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\le\pi_0\}\) and \(D^+:=\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\ge\pi_0+1\}\). A split inference may append any inequality valid for \(\operatorname{conv}((P\cap D^-)\cup(P\cap D^+))\). A split proof is a finite sequence of such inferences, with each current relaxation including all previously appended inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split proof derives inequalities from the convex hull of the two sides of an integer split disjunction and adds them sequentially to the relaxation.

children.title: General Disjunctive Proof Systems
children.top_down_role: Certificates derived from disjunction families broader than splits.

knowledge_statements.title: General Disjunctive Proof Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite valid disjunctions over a convex polyhedral relaxation; the formulation includes split proofs as a two-term special case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) denote the mixed-integer domain, let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a rational polyhedron, and suppose \(X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^qD_j\) for a finite family of sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_q\subseteq\mathbb R^n\). Set \[Q:=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^q(P\cap D_j)\right).\] A general disjunctive inference appends any inequality valid for \(Q\). It is sound because \(P\cap X_I\subseteq Q\subseteq P\). A disjunctive proof is a finite sequence of these inferences, recording each disjunction and enough data to verify validity of the derived inequality for its disjunctive hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A general disjunctive proof derives inequalities from the convex hull of a convex polyhedral relaxation intersected with every term of a finite disjunction valid for the mixed-integer domain.
assumptions_latex: The current relaxation \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is a rational polyhedron.
The finite disjunction \(D_1\cup\cdots\cup D_q\) contains every point of the mixed-integer domain \(X_I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P\cap X_I\subseteq\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{j=1}^q(P\cap D_j)\right)\subseteq P.\]

notation.meaning: Disjunctive hull for the current relaxation

children.title: Proof-System Simulation
children.top_down_role: Relative simulation power across split-based and general disjunctive systems.

assumptions_latex: Proofs and instances have fixed finite encodings.
The simulation preserves the final certified inequality or contradiction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{size}_{\mathsf T}(I,C)\le p\bigl(\operatorname{size}_{\mathsf S}(I,C)+|I|\bigr)\] for some polynomial \(p\) whenever \(C\) has an \(\mathsf S\)-proof.

notation.meaning: Minimum encoded proof size of certificate C

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Polynomial simulation is the standard proof-complexity comparison after fixing encodings and proof size.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial simulation by total encoded proof size; rank-preserving simulation is a stronger separate notion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proof system \(\mathsf T\) polynomially simulates \(\mathsf S\) if there is a polynomial \(p\) such that, for every encoded instance \(I\) and every conclusion \(C\) having an \(\mathsf S\)-proof, \[\operatorname{size}_{\mathsf T}(I,C)\le p\bigl(|I|+\operatorname{size}_{\mathsf S}(I,C)\bigr).\] The translated \(\mathsf T\)-proof must certify the same \(C\). Mutual polynomial simulation is polynomial equivalence. Any claim of simulation must specify whether size counts lines, symbols, coefficient bits, or their total.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One proof system polynomially simulates another when every proof can be translated to the same conclusion with only polynomial growth in encoded size.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-System Simulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent after fixing encodings and total proof size, but no source supports this cutting-plane-specific simulation convention.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Proof-Measure Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Principal size measures for cutting-plane derivations.

children.title: Proof Rank
children.top_down_role: Round or depth complexity of cutting-plane derivations.

assumptions_latex: A cutting-plane proof is represented as a directed acyclic derivation graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{rank}(\Pi):=\max_{v\in V(\Pi)}d(v),\qquad d(v):=1+\max_{u\in\operatorname{pred}(v)}d(u)\] for derived lines.

notation.meaning: Premise lines used directly to infer v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Proof rank is derivation depth once the inference DAG and initial depth convention are fixed.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic derivation depth; equality with closure rank requires an additional system-specific theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a derivation DAG \(\Pi\), assign \(d(v):=0\) to every initial inequality. For a derived line \(v\), define \[d(v):=1+\max\{d(u):u\in\operatorname{pred}(v)\}.\] The proof rank is \(\operatorname{rank}(\Pi):=\max_{v\in V(\Pi)}d(v)\), or the depth of the designated final line when only one conclusion is measured. Independent inferences may occupy the same rank, so rank measures sequential dependence rather than the number of lines.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof rank is the maximum number of dependent inference layers from an initial inequality to a derived line or designated conclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof Rank

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The derivation-depth definition is internally consistent and properly distinguished from closure rank, but no source establishes this proof-rank convention for the intended cutting-plane systems.

children.title: Proof Length
children.top_down_role: Number of derived inequalities or inference stages in a certificate.

assumptions_latex: A proof is a finite sequence or directed acyclic graph of inference lines.
The convention for counting initial and repeated lines is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{len}(\Pi):=|V_{\mathrm{der}}(\Pi)|.\]
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Line count is the standard proof-length measure after an explicit counting convention is fixed.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Line-count length; total bit or symbol size must be reported separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the derived-line convention, the length of a cutting-plane proof \(\Pi\) is \[\operatorname{len}(\Pi):=|V_{\mathrm{der}}(\Pi)|,\] where \(V_{\mathrm{der}}(\Pi)\) contains every inference line not present in the initial formulation. If the same inequality is derived twice, both occurrences count unless proofs are canonically represented as DAGs with shared nodes. Proof length alone ignores the bit length of coefficients, multipliers, and annotations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof length counts derived inference lines under a fixed convention; it does not by itself measure coefficient sizes or total encoded proof size.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof Length

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The derived-line convention is precise and fits the leaf, but it is convention-dependent and has no citation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-matrix bound on cutting-plane proof length
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound depends only on the rational matrix A and is uniform over the rational right-hand side b and every integral-coefficient inequality valid for the integer solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every rational matrix \(A\), there exists a number \(t(A)\) such that, if \(Ax\le b\) is a rational system having at least one integral solution, \(c\) is integral, and \(cx\le\delta\) holds for every integral solution of \(Ax\le b\), then \(cx\le\delta\) has a cutting-plane proof from \(Ax\le b\) of length at most \(t(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each rational matrix A, one bound depending only on A limits the cutting-plane proof length of every integral-coefficient inequality valid for the integer solutions of any integer-feasible rational system Ax ≤ b.
assumptions_latex: Ax\le b\text{ is a rational system}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{length}_{\mathrm{CP}}(Ax\le b\vdash cx\le\delta)\le t(A)

children.title: Coefficient Complexity
children.top_down_role: Encoding scale of coefficients appearing in cutting-plane derivations.

assumptions_latex: Every proof line and inference multiplier is rationally encoded in binary.
Each rational is stored as a reduced numerator-denominator pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{coef}(\Pi):=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q(\Pi)}\bigl(\lceil\log_2(|\operatorname{num}(q)|+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(\operatorname{den}(q)+1)\rceil\bigr).\]

notation.meaning: Set of rational coefficients and multipliers occurring in the proof

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Binary numerator-denominator length is the standard encoding measure for rational coefficients.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum per-rational bit complexity; total proof encoding size is a separate aggregate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Q(\Pi)\) contain every rational coefficient, right-hand side, and inference multiplier explicitly appearing in \(\Pi\). Write each \(q\in\mathcal Q(\Pi)\) as a reduced fraction with positive denominator. Its binary size is \[\ell(q):=\lceil\log_2(|\operatorname{num}(q)|+1)\rceil+\lceil\log_2(\operatorname{den}(q)+1)\rceil.\] The coefficient complexity of \(\Pi\) is \(\operatorname{coef}(\Pi):=\max_{q\in\mathcal Q(\Pi)}\ell(q)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coefficient complexity is the largest binary encoding length of any rational coefficient, right-hand side, or multiplier explicitly appearing in the proof.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Complexity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The maximum binary rational-size measure is precise under the stated normalization, but no source supports this particular coefficient-complexity convention.

children.title: Proof-Measure Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs among depth, length, and coefficient size.

assumptions_latex: A proof system \(\mathsf S\), instance \(I\), and required conclusion \(C\) are fixed.
Rank, length, and coefficient complexity use fixed encoding conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[L_{\mathsf S}(I,C;r,b)\text{ is nonincreasing separately in }r\text{ and }b.\]

notation.meaning: Admissible proofs of C from I in system S

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: A constrained minimum and its Pareto frontier formally encode tradeoffs among proof measures.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A neutral Pareto representation; it does not assert a particular lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the constrained proof-length function by \[L_{\mathsf S}(I,C;r,b):=\min\{\operatorname{len}(\Pi):\Pi\in\mathcal P_{\mathsf S}(I,C),\ \operatorname{rank}(\Pi)\le r,\ \operatorname{coef}(\Pi)\le b\},\] with the minimum equal to \(+\infty\) when the feasible set is empty. Increasing either budget cannot increase this minimum. The nondominated triples \((\operatorname{rank}(\Pi),\operatorname{len}(\Pi),\operatorname{coef}(\Pi))\) form the proof-measure Pareto frontier; a tradeoff lower bound excludes a specified region beneath that frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proof-measure tradeoffs are represented by minimizing proof length subject to rank and coefficient budgets, or equivalently by the nondominated triples of all three measures.
knowledge_statements.title: Proof-Measure Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained minimum and Pareto-frontier representation are mathematically coherent and do not overstate a lower bound, but no source is supplied for this proof-measure framework.

children.title: Cutting-Plane Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Families exhibiting large depth, length, or coefficient requirements.

assumptions_latex: The cutting-plane proof model permits integer linear inequalities derived by nonnegative linear combination and integer rounding.
Proof length is the number of derived inequalities, and coefficient size is measured in binary encoding length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is a constant \(c>0\) and a family \((F_n)_{n\ge 1}\) of infeasible \(0\)-\(1\) integer-linear systems having polynomial encoding size such that every cutting-plane refutation of \(F_n\) has length at least \(2^{cn}\), or else must use an inequality whose coefficient encoding length is superpolynomial in \(n\).

notation.meaning: The infeasible integer-linear instance indexed by size parameter n.
A positive absolute constant independent of n.

review_flags: Exact hard family and cutting-plane inference variant require an authoritative proof-complexity source.
The length-versus-coefficient tradeoff may require separation into model-specific statements.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential lower-bound form; the precise proof-system variant remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider cutting-plane refutations of infeasible \(0\)-\(1\) integer-linear systems, where lines are integer linear inequalities and inference uses nonnegative linear combination followed by sound integer rounding. Measure length by the number of derived lines and coefficient complexity by total binary encoding length. There is a constant \(c>0\) and a polynomial-size family \((F_n)_{n\ge 1}\) for which every refutation either contains at least \(2^{cn}\) lines or contains a line with superpolynomial coefficient encoding length. Thus short proofs cannot simultaneously retain polynomially bounded coefficients on this family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Some polynomial-size infeasible 0–1 systems force cutting-plane refutations to have exponentially many lines or coefficients of superpolynomial encoding length.
knowledge_statements.title: Cutting-Plane Lower Bounds

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact cutting-planes inference system, hard family, and asserted length-versus-coefficient tradeoff are source-dependent and cannot be validated without an authoritative theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of full-dimensional maximal lattice-free convex sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral, facet-contact, and recession structure of full-dimensional maximal lattice-free convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) be full-dimensional. Then \(K\) is a maximal lattice-free convex set if and only if \(K\) is a polyhedron, \(\operatorname{int}(K)\cap\mathbb{Z}^p=\varnothing\), and \(\operatorname{relint}(F)\cap\mathbb{Z}^p\neq\varnothing\) for every facet \(F\) of \(K\). Furthermore, if \(K\) is a maximal lattice-free convex set, then \(\operatorname{rec}(K)=\operatorname{lin}(K)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional set is a maximal lattice-free convex set exactly when it is a lattice-free polyhedron whose every facet contains an integer point in its relative interior. Such a set has recession cone equal to its lineality space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ is maximal lattice-free and convex}\iff\left(K\text{ is a polyhedron},\ \operatorname{int}(K)\cap\mathbb{Z}^p=\varnothing,\ \forall F\in\operatorname{Facets}(K),\ \operatorname{relint}(F)\cap\mathbb{Z}^p\neq\varnothing\right);\quad K\text{ maximal lattice-free and convex}\Rightarrow\operatorname{rec}(K)=\operatorname{lin}(K)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximal mixed-integer-free convex sets and maximal extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combines maximality relative to the stated admissible class, existence of maximal extensions, and the source's intersection-cut reduction, which also depends on its referenced Remark 6.6.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \bar{x}\in\mathbb{R}^n and let M:=\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^{n-p}. A closed convex set C satisfying \bar{x}\in\operatorname{int}(C) and \operatorname{int}(C)\cap M=\varnothing is maximal if there is no closed convex C'\supsetneq C satisfying the same properties. Every such C is contained in a maximal such set. Together with the intersection-cut property referenced in Remark 6.6, this implies that it suffices to consider intersection cuts defined by maximal members of this class.

Every admissible set has a maximal extension; with the cited cut-comparison property, intersection-cut generation can therefore be restricted to maximal sets.

assumptions_latex: The set \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is full-dimensional, closed, convex, and lattice-free.
The set \(L\) is inclusion-maximal among lattice-free convex sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The set \(L\) is a polyhedron, and every facet \(F\) satisfies \(\operatorname{relint}(F)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\ne\varnothing\). Consequently, moving any facet outward admits an integer point to the interior.

auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full-dimensional Euclidean lattice setting; each facet is blocked by an integer boundary point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a full-dimensional, closed, convex set with \(\operatorname{int}(L)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\varnothing\), maximal under inclusion with this property. Then \(L\) is polyhedral and, for every facet \(F\) of \(L\), one has \(\operatorname{relint}(F)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\ne\varnothing\). knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be full-dimensional, closed, convex, and lattice-free, meaning \(\operatorname{int}(L)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\varnothing\). children.title: Boundary-Lattice Witnesses

children.top_down_role: Unbounded directions and lattice subspaces of maximal lattice-free sets.

children.title: Recession Cones
children.top_down_role: Unbounded directions of maximal lattice-free sets.

assumptions_latex: The set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recession cone is \(\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^d:x+\lambda r\in C\text{ for every }x\in C,\ \lambda\ge0\}\), a closed convex cone independent of the chosen base point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard recession cone of a nonempty closed convex set.

source_refs.locator: 3.5.1 Minkowski-Weyl Theorem for Polyhedral Cones p. 94

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\), its recession cone is
\[\operatorname{rec}(C)=\{r\in\mathbb{R}^d:x+\lambda r\in C\text{ for every }x\in C\text{ and every }\lambda\ge0\}.\]
Equivalently, it suffices to impose the ray condition for one point \(x\in C\). The set \(\operatorname{rec}(C)\) is a closed convex cone and records exactly the directions along which \(C\) is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone consists of directions along which every point of a closed convex set can be translated indefinitely while remaining in the set.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession Cones

source_witnesses.locator: 3.5.1 Minkowski-Weyl Theorem for Polyhedral Cones p. 94

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and properties are standard, but the cited Minkowski–Weyl subsection for polyhedral cones does not specifically support the recession cone of an arbitrary nonempty closed convex set or the one-base-point equivalence.

children.title: Lattice Subspaces
children.top_down_role: Linear subspaces compatible with the ambient lattice.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A linear subspace \(W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a lattice subspace exactly when \(W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}(W\cap\mathbb{Z}^d)\); equivalently, \(W\) has a basis of integer vectors.

notation.meaning: A linear subspace of the ambient Euclidean space.
The integer lattice contained in W.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard rational-subspace characterization relative to the integer lattice
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lattice subspaces relative to the standard integer lattice; also called rational subspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A linear subspace \(W\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a lattice subspace relative to \(\mathbb{Z}^d\) if
\[W=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}(W\cap\mathbb{Z}^d).\]
Equivalently, \(W\) admits a basis consisting of vectors in \(\mathbb{Z}^d\), and \(W\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\) is a full-rank lattice in \(W\). This condition is also equivalent to rationality of the subspace with respect to the standard coordinate system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lattice subspace is a linear subspace spanned by its integer vectors, equivalently one having an integer-vector basis.
knowledge_statements.title: Lattice Subspaces

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equivalent characterizations of a lattice subspace are standard and appropriately presented as a definition, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Recession–Lattice Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Restrictions linking unbounded directions to lattice-supported subspaces.

assumptions_latex: The set \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is full-dimensional and maximal lattice-free.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recession cone \(\operatorname{rec}(L)\) is a lattice subspace: it is a linear space and \(\operatorname{rec}(L)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}(\operatorname{rec}(L)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: structural theorem for full-dimensional maximal lattice-free sets
Check whether the intended local convention assumes closed convex sets throughout.
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility theorem for recession directions of full-dimensional maximal lattice-free sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a full-dimensional maximal lattice-free closed convex set. Then its recession cone is not merely a convex cone: \(\operatorname{rec}(L)\) is a linear subspace and is rational with respect to the integer lattice. Explicitly,
\[\operatorname{rec}(L)=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb{R}}\bigl(\operatorname{rec}(L)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d\bigr).\]
Thus every unbounded direction is contained in a recession space generated by integer directions, and \(L\) is invariant under translation by that entire space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The recession cone of a full-dimensional maximal lattice-free set is a linear subspace generated by integer directions.
knowledge_statements.title: Recession–Lattice Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The structural claim about recession spaces of full-dimensional maximal lattice-free sets is plausible and locally appropriate, but it requires an authoritative theorem citation covering closed convex sets and the rational-subspace conclusion.

children.title: Lattice-Free Rational Polyhedrality Regimes

children.title: Rational Lattice-Free Regions
children.top_down_role: Rational descriptions of maximal lattice-free regions.

assumptions_latex: The region \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a full-dimensional polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The region \(P\) is rational lattice-free when it has a description \(P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\le b\}\) with \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times d}\), \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), and \(\operatorname{int}(P)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: A rational inequality description of P.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard conjunction of rational polyhedrality and lattice-freeness
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rationality is attached to a finite inequality description of the region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A full-dimensional region \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is a rational lattice-free region if there exist \(A\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times d}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{Q}^m\) such that
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Ax\le b\}\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{int}(P)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\varnothing.\]
Equivalently, after multiplying rows by positive integers, \(P\) has a finite inequality description with integral coefficients and contains no integer point in its Euclidean interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rational lattice-free region is a rational polyhedron whose Euclidean interior contains no integer point.
knowledge_statements.title: Rational Lattice-Free Regions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is precise and distinguishes rational polyhedrality from lattice-freeness, but it has no supporting source with a specific locator.

children.title: Polyhedral Lattice-Free Regions
children.top_down_role: Finite-facet structure of maximal lattice-free regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Polyhedral Lattice-Free Regions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Real polyhedrality without a rationality requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A full-dimensional convex region \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is polyhedral lattice-free if there are finitely many vectors \(a_i\in\mathbb{R}^d\) and scalars \(\beta_i\in\mathbb{R}\), indexed by \(i=1,\ldots,m\), such that
\[P=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:a_i^\top x\le\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\]
and \(\operatorname{int}(P)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\varnothing\). No rationality of the data is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polyhedral lattice-free region is a finite intersection of real halfspaces whose Euclidean interior contains no integer point; its coefficients need not be rational.
assumptions_latex: The region \(P\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) is full-dimensional and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The region \(P\) is polyhedral lattice-free exactly when \(P=\{x:a_i^\top x\le\beta_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) for finitely many real inequalities and \(\operatorname{int}(P)\cap\mathbb{Z}^d=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: The finite real inequality data indexed by i.

review_flags: The previously cited Minkowski–Weyl subsection does not specifically support the lattice-free definition.

children.title: Nonpolyhedral Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where standard finite polyhedral conclusions require modification.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonpolyhedral lattice-free closed convex sets exist, but no full-dimensional one is inclusion-maximal lattice-free; maximality forces polyhedrality.

notation.meaning: The closed Euclidean ball centered at c with radius r.
The half-integral center used in the example.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit nonpolyhedral lattice-free example combined with the classical maximality criterion
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonpolyhedral lattice-free sets exist below maximality, but not as full-dimensional maximal regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(c=(1/2,1/2)\) and choose \(0<r<1/\sqrt{2}\). The closed Euclidean ball \(B(c,r)\) is full-dimensional, convex, nonpolyhedral, and lattice-free because every point of \(\mathbb{Z}^2\) has distance at least \(1/\sqrt{2}\) from \(c\). Nevertheless, \(B(c,r)\) is not maximal lattice-free. More generally, a full-dimensional maximal lattice-free closed convex set in \(\mathbb{R}^d\) must be polyhedral; hence curved or infinitely faceted boundaries occur only before maximal extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonpolyhedral lattice-free convex regions exist, such as small balls centered at half-integral points, but full-dimensional maximal lattice-free sets must be polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonpolyhedral Boundary Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ball example and the boundary between nonmaximal nonpolyhedral sets and maximal polyhedral sets are mathematically coherent and fit a failure-boundary leaf, but the general maximality assertion needs a cited theorem locator.

children.title: Splits
children.top_down_role: The fundamental one-dimensional lattice-free family.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The slab \(S(\pi,k)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:k\le\pi^\top x\le k+1\}\) is a full-dimensional maximal lattice-free set called a split.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition of a split in integer optimization
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed split slab for the standard integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\pi\in\mathbb{Z}^d\) be primitive, meaning that the greatest common divisor of its coordinates is one, and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}\). The set
\[S(\pi,k)=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:k\le\pi^\top x\le k+1\}\]
is called a split. Its interior contains no integer point because \(\pi^\top z\in\mathbb{Z}\) for every \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^d\). Both boundary hyperplanes contain integer points, and primitiveness implies that the slab is a full-dimensional maximal lattice-free convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split is the unit-width slab between two consecutive lattice hyperplanes with a primitive integer normal; it is maximal lattice-free.
knowledge_statements.title: Splits

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primitive unit-width slab is the standard split and the maximal lattice-free conclusion is appropriate, but no authoritative source locator is supplied.

children.title: Lattice-Free Triangles
children.top_down_role: Triangle families in two-row lattice-free geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice-Free Triangles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Planar maximal lattice-free triangles, without subdividing the three standard triangle types.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\) be a full-dimensional triangular region satisfying \(\operatorname{int}(T)\cap\mathbb{Z}^2=\varnothing\). Then \(T\) is maximal lattice-free if and only if every edge \(E\) of \(T\) contains an integer point in its relative interior:
\[\operatorname{relint}(E)\cap\mathbb{Z}^2\ne\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A full-dimensional planar lattice-free triangle is maximal lattice-free exactly when the relative interior of each of its three edges contains an integer point.
assumptions_latex: The set \(T\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\) is a full-dimensional triangle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The triangle \(T\) is maximal lattice-free if and only if every edge \(E\) satisfies \(\operatorname{relint}(E)\cap\mathbb{Z}^2\ne\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: A full-dimensional lattice-free triangular region in the plane.

review_flags: Detailed Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 subdivision is outside this compact record.

Then \(Q\) is maximal lattice-free with respect to \(\mathbb{Z}^2\) if and only if \(\operatorname{int}(Q)\cap\mathbb{Z}^2=\varnothing\) and the relative interior of each of its four edges contains an integer point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A planar quadrilateral is maximal lattice-free exactly when its interior has no integer point and every edge contains an integer point in its relative interior.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^2\) is a full-dimensional closed convex quadrilateral.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher-Dimensional Lattice-Free Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural theorem for full-dimensional maximal lattice-free convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be full-dimensional, closed, convex, and maximal among convex sets satisfying \(\operatorname{int}(B)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n=\varnothing\). Then \(B\) is a polyhedron; the relative interior of every facet of \(B\) contains a point of \(\mathbb{Z}^n\); \(B\) has at most \(2^n\) facets; and \(\operatorname{rec}(B)\) is a linear subspace generated by integer vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every full-dimensional maximal lattice-free convex set is polyhedral, has an integer point inside each facet, has at most 2^n facets, and has rational linear recession.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is full-dimensional, closed, convex, lattice-free, and inclusion-maximal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\) is polyhedral with at most \(2^n\) facets, every facet contains a relative-interior lattice point, and \(\operatorname{rec}(B)\) is integer-generated linear.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical structure theorem for maximal lattice-free convex sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bundled structural claims are plausible and fit higher-dimensional lattice-free geometry, but their exact hypotheses and conclusions require an authoritative theorem locator.

children.title: Mixed-Lattice-Free Sets
children.top_down_role: Forbidden regions relative to mixed continuous-discrete lattices.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Lattice-Free Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lattice-freeness relative to integer and continuous coordinate blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix integers \(p\geq1\) and \(q\geq0\), and let \(M=\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p+q}\). A full-dimensional convex set \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p+q}\) is mixed-lattice-free if \(\operatorname{int}(B)\cap M=\varnothing\). It is maximal mixed-lattice-free if no convex set properly containing \(B\) has this property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-lattice-free convex set has no point with integral first-coordinate block in its interior; maximality means that no proper convex enlargement preserves this exclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\text{ is mixed-lattice-free}\iff\operatorname{int}(B)\cap(\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^q)=\varnothing\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: direct specialization of S-free-set terminology

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the terminal container, but the full-dimensional convention and maximality formulation are convention-sensitive and uncited.

children.title: S-Free Sets
children.top_down_role: Forbidden regions relative to a prescribed discrete set.

knowledge_statements.title: S-Free Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex sets whose interiors avoid a prescribed forbidden set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\). A full-dimensional convex set \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is \(S\)-free if \(\operatorname{int}(B)\cap S=\varnothing\). It is maximal \(S\)-free if it is \(S\)-free and every convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) satisfying \(B\subsetneq C\) has \(\operatorname{int}(C)\cap S\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An S-free convex set has an interior disjoint from S. It is maximal when every proper convex enlargement places some point of S in the interior.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B\text{ is }S\text{-free}\iff\operatorname{int}(B)\cap S=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: prescribed forbidden subset of the ambient space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard definition in cut-generating-function theory

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is a coherent definition of full-dimensional S-free sets, but no source establishes that this is the intended local convention.

children.title: Mixed-Lattice Specialization
children.top_down_role: Placement of mixed-lattice geometry within the broader S-free framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Lattice Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cylinder representation of maximal mixed-lattice-free convex sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=\mathbb{Z}^p\times\mathbb{R}^q\), and let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p+q}\) be a full-dimensional maximal \(M\)-free closed convex set. Then there exists a full-dimensional maximal lattice-free closed convex set \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) such that \(B=C\times\mathbb{R}^q\). Conversely, every set of this product form is maximal \(M\)-free.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximal mixed-lattice-free convex sets are precisely cylinders over maximal lattice-free sets in the integer-coordinate space.
assumptions_latex: \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{p+q}\) is full-dimensional, closed, convex, and maximal \(M\)-free.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B=C\times\mathbb{R}^q\) for some maximal lattice-free \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\), and every such product is maximal \(M\)-free.

notation.meaning: maximal lattice-free base in the integer-coordinate space

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: invariance along continuous mixed-lattice directions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cylinder representation fits the specialization container, but its maximality equivalence is nontrivial and needs a precise supporting theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trivial and nontrivial corner-polyhedron inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents corner-polyhedron inequalities in nonbasic variables and characterizes those implied solely by nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After substituting the basic-variable equations, every valid linear inequality for \(\operatorname{corner}(B)\) can be expressed as \(\sum_{j\in N}\gamma_jx_j\ge\delta\). Such an inequality is trivial, meaning that it is implied by \(x_j\ge0\) for all \(j\in N\), if and only if \(\gamma_j\ge0\) for every \(j\in N\) and \(\delta\le0\). It is nontrivial otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every valid linear inequality for a corner polyhedron can be written using only nonbasic variables. It is trivial precisely when all coefficients are nonnegative and its right-hand side is nonpositive; otherwise it is nontrivial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \left(\sum_{j\in N}\gamma_jx_j\ge\delta\text{ is implied by }x_N\ge0\right)\iff\left(\gamma_j\ge0\ \forall j\in N\text{ and }\delta\le0\right).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dominance of normalized corner inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines dominance over the nonnegative orthant and gives its coefficientwise characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \sum_{j\in N}\gamma_jx_j\ge1 and \sum_{j\in N}\gamma'_jx_j\ge1 be valid inequalities for \operatorname{corner}(B). The first dominates the second if every x\in\mathbb{R}_+^n satisfying \sum_{j\in N}\gamma'_jx_j\ge1 also satisfies \sum_{j\in N}\gamma_jx_j\ge1. This holds if and only if \gamma_j\le\gamma'_j for every j\in N.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among normalized valid corner inequalities, the first dominates the second when its feasible halfspace over the nonnegative orthant contains the second one's feasible halfspace. This is equivalent to every coefficient of the first being no larger than the corresponding coefficient of the second.

children.title: Pure-Integer Corner Polyhedra
children.top_down_role: Corner structure with fully integral basic rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Pure-Integer Corner Polyhedra
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite pure-integer corner polyhedron induced by nonbasic rays.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in\mathbb{R}^m\setminus\mathbb{Z}^m\) and \(R=[r^1,\ldots,r^k]\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times k}\). The pure-integer corner relaxation is \(X_I(f,R)=\{s\in\mathbb{Z}_+^k:f+Rs\in\mathbb{Z}^m\}\). Its corner polyhedron is \(P_I(f,R)=\operatorname{conv}(X_I(f,R))\subseteq\mathbb{R}^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The pure-integer corner polyhedron is the convex hull of nonnegative integer ray multipliers that restore integrality to a fractional basic vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_I(f,R)=\operatorname{conv}\{s\in\mathbb{Z}_+^k:f+Rs\in\mathbb{Z}^m\}\).

notation.meaning: matrix of finitely many corner rays

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite pure-integer corner-polyhedron definition is internally consistent and locally appropriate, but no inspectable definition is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gomory’s master corner-polyhedron facet characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes right-hand-side-one facets of a finite pure-integer master corner polyhedron through the vertices of a coefficient polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\widetilde a_1,\ldots,\widetilde a_N\) be the columns of the master matrix \(\widetilde A\). The inequality \(y^Tx\ge1\) determines a facet of \(P(\widetilde A,b)\) if and only if \(y=(\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_N)^T\) is a vertex of
\[
Q=\left\{\eta\in\mathbb R_+^N:\begin{array}{ll}
\eta_i+\eta_j\ge\eta_k&\text{if }\widetilde a_i+\widetilde a_j\equiv\widetilde a_k\pmod1,\\
\eta_i+\eta_j=1&\text{if }\widetilde a_i+\widetilde a_j\equiv b\pmod1,\\
\eta_k=1&\text{if }\widetilde a_k\equiv b\pmod1
\end{array}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inequality with right-hand side one defines a facet of the master corner polyhedron exactly when its coefficient vector is a vertex of the nonnegative polytope specified by the residue-class subadditivity, complementarity, and normalization conditions.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Corner Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-column representation of a corner relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite ray sets \(R_I=\{r^1,\ldots,r^k\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(R_C=\{q^1,\ldots,q^\ell\}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), the finite corner model at \(f\notin\mathbb{Z}^m\) consists of \((s,y)\in\mathbb{Z}_+^k\times\mathbb{R}_+^\ell\) satisfying \(f+\sum_{j=1}^k r^js_j+\sum_{j=1}^\ell q^jy_j\in\mathbb{Z}^m\). Its convexified model is the convex hull of these finitely indexed feasible vectors.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite mixed-integer corner polyhedron and its linear relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the finite corner model associated with a feasible integer-basic basis and records the vertex-and-rays representation of its linear relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{x:Ax=b,\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ x_i\ge0\ (i=1,\ldots,n)\}\), where \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(p\le n\). For a feasible basis \(B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}\), let \(N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\) and write \(x_i=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j\) for \(i\in B\). The corner polyhedron is \[\operatorname{corner}(B)=\operatorname{conv}\left\{x:x_i=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j\ (i\in B),\ x_i\in\mathbb Z\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ x_j\ge0\ (j\in N)\right\}.\] It contains \(S\), so every inequality valid for \(\operatorname{corner}(B)\) is valid for \(S\). Its linear relaxation \(P(B)\) has the unique vertex \(\bar x\), with \(\bar x_i=\bar b_i\) for \(i\in B\) and \(\bar x_j=0\) for \(j\in N\), and \[P(B)=\{\bar x\}+\operatorname{cone}\{\bar r^j:j\in N\},\] where \(\bar r_h^j=-\bar a_{hj}\) for \(h\in B\), \(\bar r_j^j=1\), and \(\bar r_h^j=0\) for \(h\in N\setminus\{j\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dropping nonnegativity on the integer basic variables produces the finite corner relaxation, whose convex hull is the corner polyhedron. This relaxes the original mixed-integer set. Its linear relaxation consists of one basic vertex plus a recession cone with one explicitly described extreme ray for each nonbasic variable.
assumptions_latex: p\le n,\quad A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb Q^m,\quad \operatorname{rank}(A)=m
B\text{ is a feasible basis},\quad B\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\},\quad N=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B
x_i=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j\ (i\in B),\quad \bar b_i\ge0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S\subseteq\operatorname{corner}(B),\qquad P(B)=\{\bar x\}+\operatorname{cone}\{\bar r^j:j\in N\},\qquad \operatorname{extremeRays}(\operatorname{rec}P(B))=\{\bar r^j:j\in N\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Additivity condition forcing equality of mixed-relaxation components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A pointwise consequence of tight additivity for a minimal valid pair in the mixed infinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\pi,\psi)\) be a minimal valid function for \(M_f\), and let \(r^*\in\mathbb{R}^q\). If there exists \(z\in\mathbb{Z}^q\) such that \[\psi(r^*)+\psi(z-f-r^*)=\psi(z-f)=1,\] then \[\pi(r^*)=\psi(r^*)=\inf_{w\in\mathbb{Z}^q}\psi(r^*+w).\]

knowledge_statements.title: Finite–Infinite Correspondence

children.title: Continuous Infinite Relaxation

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Infinite Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-variable form of the infinite group relaxation over the lattice quotient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(f\in\mathbb R^q\setminus\mathbb Z^q\). The continuous infinite relaxation is
\[
R_f^{\mathrm C}:=\left\{y:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R_+:\ |\operatorname{supp}(y)|<\infty,\quad \sum_{r\in\mathbb R^q}r\,y(r)\in f+\mathbb Z^q\right\}.
\]
A coefficient function \(\pi:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R\) defines a valid normalized inequality when
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathbb R^q}\pi(r)y(r)\ge 1
\]
for every \(y\in R_f^{\mathrm C}\). Finite support makes both displayed sums finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative, finitely supported continuous weights combine their indexed vectors to a point congruent to the fixed fractional vector modulo the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_f^{\mathrm C}\) is the continuous infinite group relaxation associated with \(f\).

notation.meaning: Set of indices at which y is nonzero.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-support formulation of the continuous infinite group relaxation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind and finite-support formulation fit the continuous infinite-relaxation container, but the record has no citation and the supplied local inventory contains no inspectable source for this specialized group-relaxation definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Infinite Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Infinite group relaxation containing both nonnegative integer and continuous variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(f\in\mathbb R^q\setminus\mathbb Z^q\). The mixed-integer infinite relaxation is
\[
R_f^{\mathrm{MI}}:=\left\{(x,y):\begin{array}{l}x:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb Z_+,\ y:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R_+,\\ |\operatorname{supp}(x)\cup\operatorname{supp}(y)|<\infty,\\ \displaystyle\sum_r r x(r)+\sum_r r y(r)\in f+\mathbb Z^q\end{array}\right\}.
\]
A pair \((\pi,\psi)\) is a normalized valid coefficient pair if
\[
\sum_r\pi(r)x(r)+\sum_r\psi(r)y(r)\ge1
\]
for every \((x,y)\in R_f^{\mathrm{MI}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finitely supported integer and continuous nonnegative weights jointly produce a vector congruent to the fixed fractional vector modulo the lattice.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_f^{\mathrm{MI}}\) combines the pure-integer and continuous infinite group structures.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard mixed-integer infinite group formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the mixed-integer infinite-relaxation container, and the integer and continuous function domains are distinguished consistently. No cited source supports the exact formulation or normalized coefficient-pair convention.

children.title: Subadditive Dual Functions

knowledge_statements.title: Subadditive Dual Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized subadditive functions generating valid inequalities for the continuous infinite group relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(f\in\mathbb R^q\setminus\mathbb Z^q\), a normalized subadditive dual function is a map \(\pi:\mathbb R^q\to\mathbb R_+\) satisfying
\[
\pi(0)=0,\qquad \pi(u+v)\le\pi(u)+\pi(v),\qquad \pi(u+z)=\pi(u),\qquad \pi(f)=1
\]
for all \(u,v\in\mathbb R^q\) and \(z\in\mathbb Z^q\). Consequently, every \(y\in R_f^{\mathrm C}\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{r\in\mathbb R^q}\pi(r)y(r)\ge1.
\]
Thus \(\pi\) is a functional certificate for a valid inequality of the continuous infinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative, lattice-periodic, normalized subadditive function supplies valid coefficients for every point of the continuous infinite relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_r\pi(r)y(r)\ge1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: subadditivity and lattice periodicity yield the customary group-validity certificate
source needed to confirm the intended normalization and function class

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind fits the title, but subadditivity and lattice periodicity alone do not justify the displayed inequality for arbitrary real-valued weights in the continuous relaxation. The statement appears to blend the periodic valid-function conditions for integer variables with the coefficient class for continuous variables; a source is required to determine the intended function class and any needed homogeneity or regularity assumptions.

children.title: Superadditive Dual Functions
children.top_down_role: Superadditive functional certificates associated with primal value structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Superadditive Dual Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Superadditive functional certificates for nonnegative integer systems written with componentwise upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\) be an additive commutative monoid equipped with a translation-invariant order. A map \(F:M\to\mathbb R\) is an admissible superadditive dual function when
\[
F(0)=0,\qquad F(u+v)\ge F(u)+F(v),\qquad u\le v\Longrightarrow F(u)\le F(v).
\]
If \(a_1,\ldots,a_n,b\in M\), \(x\in\mathbb Z_+^n\), and \(\sum_{j=1}^n a_jx_j\le b\), then
\[
\sum_{j=1}^nF(a_j)x_j\le F(b).
\]
Hence evaluation of \(F\) on the columns and right-hand side produces a valid inequality for the integer system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized, order-preserving superadditive function maps an integer conic combination bounded by the right-hand side to a valid scalar inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_jF(a_j)x_j\le F(b)\).

notation.meaning: Ordered commutative monoid containing columns and right-hand sides.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard superadditive functional certificate for nonnegative integer systems
source needed to confirm the ambient ordered algebraic structure intended by the node

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition content kind is plausible, and the ordered-monoid certificate is mathematically coherent for nonnegative integer combinations. However, no citation establishes that this general ordered-monoid convention is the superadditive dual-function notion intended by the local corner-group duality container.

children.title: Functional Dual Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Transformations and equivalence regimes connecting the two functional viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Functional Dual Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-reflection equivalence between subadditive and superadditive functions on an additive group.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be an abelian group and let \(\phi:G\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(\phi(0)=0\). Define
\[
(T\phi)(u):=-\phi(-u)\qquad(u\in G).
\]
Then \(T\) is an involution, since \(T(T\phi)=\phi\), and
\[
\phi(u+v)\le\phi(u)+\phi(v)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(T\phi)(u+v)\ge(T\phi)(u)+(T\phi)(v).
\]
Thus sign-reflection bijectively converts normalized subadditive functions into normalized superadditive functions. Any additional periodicity with respect to a subgroup \(H\le G\) is preserved by \(T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negating both the argument and value gives an involutive bijection between normalized subadditive and superadditive functions, preserving subgroup periodicity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\phi\) is subadditive if and only if \(T\phi\) is superadditive.
review_flags: source needed to verify that this is the chapter's intended functional-duality convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality content kind fits the terminal container, and the sign-reflection equivalence is internally consistent. No source connects this abstract involution to the chapter's intended functional dual correspondence or its relevant validity-function classes.

children.title: Gauge Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minkowski-functional representation of a closed convex neighborhood of the origin.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\). Its gauge is
\[
\gamma_C(r):=\inf\{\lambda>0:r\in\lambda C\}.
\]
The function \(\gamma_C\) is finite, positively homogeneous, and subadditive, and it represents the set by
\[
C=\{r\in\mathbb R^q:\gamma_C(r)\le1\},
\qquad
\operatorname{int}C=\{r\in\mathbb R^q:\gamma_C(r)<1\}.
\]
If the ray \(\{tr:t\ge0\}\) leaves \(C\) at \(\lambda r\), where \(\lambda>0\), then \(\gamma_C(r)=1/\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge records the reciprocal distance to a convex set's boundary along each ray and reconstructs the set as its unit sublevel set.

notation.meaning: Dilation of C by the positive scalar lambda.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind and gauge identities fit the gauge-representation leaf. The record provides no authoritative convex-analysis citation with a definition or theorem locator, and the local inventory does not supply one.

children.title: Support Representations

knowledge_statements.title: Support Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Halfspace and support-function representation through the polar of a convex neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\), and define its polar by
\[
C^\circ:=\{a\in\mathbb R^q:a^\top x\le1\text{ for every }x\in C\}.
\]
Then
\[
C=\bigcap_{a\in C^\circ}\{x\in\mathbb R^q:a^\top x\le1\}.
\]
Equivalently, membership in \(C\) is characterized by
\[
\sigma_{C^\circ}(x):=\sup_{a\in C^\circ}a^\top x\le1.
\]
Thus the supporting normals in \(C^\circ\) provide a complete halfspace representation of \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex neighborhood of the origin equals the intersection of all normalized halfspaces whose normals belong to its polar.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C=\bigcap_{a\in C^\circ}\{x:a^\top x\le1\}\).

notation.meaning: Support function of the polar set.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: bipolar and supporting-halfspace representation of a closed convex set

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation content kind fits the support-representation leaf, and the polar halfspace formulation is precise under the stated assumptions. An authoritative bipolar or support-representation locator is absent.

children.title: Gauge–Support Translation
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between gauge data and support data.

knowledge_statements.title: Gauge–Support Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality between a convex set's gauge and the support function of its polar.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) be closed and convex with \(0\in\operatorname{int}C\). For every \(r\in\mathbb R^q\),
\[
\gamma_C(r)=\sigma_{C^\circ}(r)=\sup_{a\in C^\circ}a^\top r.
\]
Consequently, an intersection-cut coefficient written as the gauge \(\gamma_C(r^j)\) can equivalently be written as the largest normalized support value \(\sup_{a\in C^\circ}a^\top r^j\). Conversely,
\[
C=\{r:\sigma_{C^\circ}(r)\le1\},
\]
so either the gauge or the polar support representation determines the same convex set and the same ray coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The gauge of a convex neighborhood equals its polar's support function, so gauge and supporting-halfspace descriptions yield identical intersection-cut coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_C=\sigma_{C^\circ}\) on \(\mathbb R^q\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The duality content kind correctly captures the gauge-support translation, and the displayed identity is consistent with the stated polar convention. No cited source supports the identity or its use for intersection-cut coefficients.

children.title: Simplicial-Cone Intersection Cuts
children.top_down_role: The classical corner-cone regime of the intersection-cut principle.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplicial-Cone Intersection Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical intersection cut for a pointed simplicial cone with apex inside a lattice-free convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
P=\left\{x=f+\sum_{j=1}^q r^js_j:s\in\mathbb R_+^q\right\},
\]
where \(f\notin\mathbb Z^q\) and the rays \(r^1,\ldots,r^q\) are linearly independent. Let \(B\) be closed, convex, lattice-free, and satisfy \(f\in\operatorname{int}B\). For each ray set
\[
\lambda_j:=\sup\{\lambda\ge0:f+\lambda r^j\in B\}.
\]
With the convention \(1/\infty=0\), every \(x\in P\cap\mathbb Z^q\), represented by \(s\), satisfies the intersection cut
\[
\sum_{j=1}^q\frac{s_j}{\lambda_j}\ge1.
\]

knowledge_statements.title: Multirow Intersection Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gauge-form intersection cut for an arbitrary finite collection of rays in multiple tableau rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\mathbb R^q\setminus\mathbb Z^q\), let \(R=[r^1\ \cdots\ r^n]\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), and impose
\[
x=f+Rs,\qquad x\in\mathbb Z^q,\qquad s\in\mathbb R_+^n.
\]
If \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is closed, convex, lattice-free, and contains \(f\) in its interior, set \(C:=B-f\). Then every feasible \((x,s)\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{j=1}^n\gamma_C(r^j)s_j\ge1.
\]
The formula permits any row dimension \(q\ge1\), any finite number of rays, and unbounded \(B\); a ray in the recession cone has coefficient zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a multirow tableau, evaluating the translated lattice-free set's gauge on each ray yields a valid intersection cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^n\gamma_{B-f}(r^j)s_j\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Translation of B placing f at the origin.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard multirow gauge-form intersection cut

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem content kind fits the multirow intersection-cut leaf, and the finite-ray gauge formula is internally consistent, including zero coefficients on recession directions. No authoritative multirow intersection-cut source or precise locator is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Facet-normal formula for multirow intersection-cut coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection cuts generated from a lattice-free polyhedron containing the reference point in its interior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^p\) be a \(\mathbb{Z}^p\)-free polyhedron with \(\bar{x}=(\bar{x}_1,\ldots,\bar{x}_p)\in\operatorname{int}(K)\), and let \(t\) be the number of facets of \(K\). Up to ordering of the facet inequalities, \(K\) has the unique normalized representation \[K=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^p:\sum_{h=1}^p d_h^i(x_h-\bar{x}_h)\leq1,\ i=1,\ldots,t\right\}.\] For \(C:=K\times\mathbb{R}^{n-p}\), the coefficients of the associated intersection cut satisfy \[\frac{1}{\alpha_j}=\max_{i=1,\ldots,t}\sum_{h=1}^p d_h^i\bar r_h^j,\qquad j\in N.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After normalizing every facet relative to the interior reference point, the facet description is unique up to ordering. Each reciprocal intersection-cut coefficient is the maximum scalar product of the corresponding ray coefficients with the normalized facet normals.
assumptions_latex: \bar r^j=(\bar r_1^j,\ldots,\bar r_p^j),\ j\in N,\text{ are the ray coefficients in the associated intersection-cut construction}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K=\left\{x\in\mathbb{R}^p:\sum_{h=1}^p d_h^i(x_h-\bar{x}_h)\leq1,\ i=1,\ldots,t\right\}\text{ uniquely up to ordering, and }\frac1{\alpha_j}=\max_{1\leq i\leq t}\sum_{h=1}^p d_h^i\bar r_h^j\quad\forall j\in N

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Intersection Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Intersection-cut validity for a general forbidden set rather than only the integer lattice.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), \(f\notin S\), and
\[
x=f+\sum_{j=1}^n r^js_j,
\qquad x\in S,
\qquad s\in\mathbb R_+^n.
\]
Suppose \(B\subseteq\mathbb R^q\) is closed and convex, \(f\in\operatorname{int}B\), and \(\operatorname{int}B\cap S=\varnothing\). For \(C:=B-f\), every feasible representation satisfies
\[
\sum_{j=1}^n\gamma_C(r^j)s_j\ge1.
\]
Thus the lattice-free construction extends to any \(S\)-free convex neighborhood of the apex; taking \(S=\mathbb Z^q\) recovers the integer multirow intersection cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the integer lattice by any forbidden set preserves the gauge cut whenever the convex neighborhood's interior avoids that set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_j\gamma_{B-f}(r^j)s_j\ge1\).

notation.meaning: Forbidden-set complement target for feasible x.
Gauge of B translated to the apex.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Validity theorem for generalized intersection cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides sufficient point, ray, and separation conditions for a generalized intersection cut valid for the mixed-integer hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a convex \(P_I\)-free set with \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}S\), and let \(C_K=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\widetilde A_Kx\geq\widetilde b_K\}\), where \(\widetilde A_K\) consists of the rows of \(\widetilde A\) indexed by \(K\), \(|K|\geq n\), and \(\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde A_K)=\operatorname{rank}(\widetilde A)\). For each extreme ray \(r^j\) originating at a vertex of \(C_K\) in \(\operatorname{int}S\), let \(p^j=r^j\cap\operatorname{bd}S\) when this intersection exists. Let \(\mathcal P\) index these intersection points and \(\mathcal R\) index the extreme rays that do not intersect \(\operatorname{bd}S\). If \(\beta\in\{1,-1\}\), \(\alpha p^j\geq\beta\) for every \(j\in\mathcal P\), \(\alpha r^j\geq0\) for every \(j\in\mathcal R\), and \(\alpha z<\beta\) for some vertex \(z\) of \(C_K\), then \(\alpha x\geq\beta\) is a valid cut for \(\operatorname{conv}(P_I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let S be a convex mixed-integer-free set containing the specified point in its interior, and construct C_K from at least n rows whose matrix has the same rank as the full matrix. Consider the boundary-intersection points of extreme rays beginning at vertices of C_K inside S and the extreme rays that never meet the boundary. For beta equal to 1 or minus 1, if alpha satisfies the stated inequalities for every such point and ray and strictly separates some vertex of C_K, then alpha x at least beta is a valid cut for the convex hull of P_I.
assumptions_latex: \widetilde A_K\text{ contains the rows of }\widetilde A\text{ indexed by }K
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha x\geq\beta\text{ is a valid cut for }\operatorname{conv}(P_I).

children.title: Generalization Strength Gaps
