knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Family Oracle Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-size obstruction for converting restricted-family membership access into separation access.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_{\mathcal F}\subseteq\mathbb Q^d\) be described by a restricted family \(\mathcal F\) of rational inequalities, and suppose an oracle answers only whether \(x\in C_{\mathcal F}\). If a separation procedure must, for every rejected query, output an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}z\le\beta\) belonging to \(\mathcal F\), then its running time is at least the binary encoding length of \((a,\beta)\). Consequently, unit-cost membership access does not imply a polynomial-time restricted-family separation oracle unless violated members of \(\mathcal F\) always possess polynomial-length encodings and can be constructively recovered from the available access model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Membership in a closure does not automatically provide a violated inequality from its defining family; long or inaccessible inequalities obstruct oracle conversion.
assumptions_latex: Queries and returned inequalities are rational and use binary encoding.
A separating output must belong to the prescribed family \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricted-family separation requires at least the output length and therefore is not implied by unit-cost membership alone.

notation.meaning: The set defined by all inequalities in the restricted family.
The prescribed family of admissible separating inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Integral-Polyhedron Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition predicate for an explicitly described rational polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), define \(P=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b\}\). The integral-polyhedron recognition problem accepts exactly when \[P=\operatorname{conv}(P\cap\mathbb Z^n).\] Equivalently, every face of \(P\) contains an integer point whenever it is nonempty; when \(P\) is a polytope, this is equivalent to every vertex of \(P\) being integral. The input is the binary encoding of \((A,b)\), so this predicate concerns the represented polyhedron rather than integrality of the displayed coefficients.

assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are rational and given explicitly in binary.

children.title: Total-Unimodularity Recognition Complexity

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Unimodularity Recognition Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-time recognition of total unimodularity for explicit matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an explicitly encoded integer matrix \(A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n}\), total-unimodularity recognition asks whether every square submatrix has determinant in \(\{0,1,-1\}\). There exists a deterministic algorithm whose running time is polynomial in \(m+n\) and the binary input length. It may first reject any entry outside \(\{0,1,-1\}\), then use the decomposition characterization of totally unimodular matrices rather than enumerate all square submatrices. The output is either acceptance or a square submatrix \(B\) satisfying \(|\det B|\ge2\), which is a polynomially verifiable rejection certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total unimodularity can be recognized in polynomial time without enumerating minors; a minor of determinant magnitude at least two certifies rejection.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) is an explicitly encoded integer matrix.
Arithmetic is measured in the standard binary bit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Total-unimodularity recognition belongs to \(\mathrm P\), and non-total-unimodularity has a square-minor certificate.

notation.meaning: A square submatrix used as a rejection certificate.

children.title: TDI Recognition Complexity
children.top_down_role: Recognition barriers for system-level total dual integrality.

knowledge_statements.title: TDI Recognition Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: TDI recognition is system-dependent and cannot be reduced to recognizing an integral feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The systems \(x\le1,-x\le0\) and \(2x\le2,-x\le0\) describe the same integral polytope \([0,1]\). The first system is totally dual integral. The second is not: for the integral objective \(c=1\), its dual is \(\min\{2y_1:2y_1-y_2=1,\ y_1,y_2\ge0\}\), whose optimum is attained at \((y_1,y_2)=(1/2,0)\) with value \(1\). Every integral dual-feasible pair has \(y_1\ge1\) and objective value at least \(2\). Hence TDI recognition must inspect the particular inequality system, not merely its polyhedron or integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two systems can define the same integral interval while only one is TDI, so TDI recognition depends on the representation.
assumptions_latex: Dual variables correspond to inequalities written in less-than-or-equal form.
TDI requires an integral optimal dual solution for every integral objective with finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Integrality of the represented polyhedron does not imply that a given description is TDI.

notation.meaning: Dual multipliers for the two inequalities.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: The claim follows by the displayed one-dimensional dual calculation.
An external source for the system-dependence of TDI remains desirable.

children.title: Normality Recognition
children.top_down_role: Complexity of recognizing saturation properties of affine semigroups or lattice polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Normality Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition predicate for normality of an explicitly generated affine semigroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb Z^d\), and define the affine semigroup \(S=\{\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i a_i:\lambda_i\in\mathbb Z_+\}\), its rational cone \(C=\{\sum_{i=1}^n\mu_i a_i:\mu_i\in\mathbb R_+\}\), and its generated group \(G=\{\sum_{i=1}^n z_i a_i:z_i\in\mathbb Z\}\). Normality recognition accepts precisely when \[S=C\cap G.\] Equivalently, whenever \(g\in G\) and \(kg\in S\) for some positive integer \(k\), one has \(g\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A generated affine semigroup is normal exactly when it contains every lattice-group point in its rational cone.
assumptions_latex: The generators \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\) are explicitly given integer vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The normality predicate is \(S=C\cap G\).

notation.meaning: The affine semigroup generated by the input vectors.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard saturation definition of a normal affine semigroup.

children.title: Integer-Decomposition Recognition
children.top_down_role: Complexity of recognizing integer-decomposition properties of polyhedra.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Decomposition Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition predicate for the integer decomposition property of a rational polytope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a rational polytope given by an explicit rational description. Integer-decomposition recognition accepts precisely when, for every integer \(k\ge1\) and every \(z\in kP\cap\mathbb Z^d\), there exist \(z_1,\ldots,z_k\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d\) such that \[z=z_1+\cdots+z_k.\] Thus the quantified dilation factor is part of the property: verifying the decomposition only for one fixed value of \(k\) does not establish the integer decomposition property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polytope has the integer decomposition property when every lattice point in every positive dilation splits into lattice points of the original polytope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(z\in kP\cap\mathbb Z^d\) decomposes into \(k\) members of \(P\cap\mathbb Z^d\) for every \(k\ge1\).

notation.meaning: The k-fold scalar dilation of P.
Lattice points of P forming the required decomposition.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: This is the standard definition of the integer decomposition property.

knowledge_statements.title: Recognition Transfer Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer between integer decomposition and normality of the homogenized lattice-point semigroup.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) be a lattice polytope and let \(S_P\subseteq\mathbb Z^{d+1}\) be generated by \(\{(x,1):x\in P\cap\mathbb Z^d\}\). Then \(P\) has the integer decomposition property if and only if \[S_P=\operatorname{cone}(S_P)\cap\mathbb Z^{d+1}.\] If additionally \(\operatorname{gp}(S_P)=\mathbb Z^{d+1}\), this is equivalent to ordinary affine-semigroup normality \(S_P=\operatorname{cone}(S_P)\cap\operatorname{gp}(S_P)\). Therefore recognition transfers directly between the two predicates only under the appropriate ambient-lattice convention or the stated full-group hypothesis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer decomposition equals ambient-lattice saturation of the homogenized semigroup; it equals ordinary semigroup normality when the generated group is the full lattice.
assumptions_latex: \(S_P\) is generated by all homogenized lattice points of \(P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\) has IDP if and only if \(S_P=\operatorname{cone}(S_P)\cap\mathbb Z^{d+1}\).

notation.meaning: The semigroup generated by homogenized lattice points of P.
The abelian group generated by the semigroup.
The real nonnegative cone generated by the semigroup.
